records.title: Classification Commands
records.text: Classification Commands. Read and edit the org's governed taxonomy — dimensions, values, and per-resource assignments — from the terminal.

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: Classification Commands
records.text:
The `classification` group (alias `class`) drives the same **governed taxonomy** as the console's
[Classification](/guides/classification) page — from the terminal. Instead of free-form tags, an
admin defines a fixed set of **dimensions** (axes) and their **allowed values** once; every resource
is then labeled from that closed vocabulary. The CLI lets you list that taxonomy, read a resource's
labels, and set or clear them.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API — it authors nothing locally. Every subcommand calls
`/cli/classification/*` with your [CLI token](/reference/cli/authentication) and operates on the **active
organization**, which you change with `alethia org switch`. Pass `--org ` to scope a single invocation to a different
organization — it is refused with `403` if you are not a member of it.

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: The model
records.text:
Three concepts, in a strict hierarchy — the CLI vocabulary matches the console's exactly:

- **Dimension** — a named axis (one question you can ask about every resource: *Environment*,
 *Team*, *Data classification*). It has a `key` slug (immutable, wire-stable), a `label`, an
 optional description, a **single/multi** mode (`Multi bool`), and an `applies_to` list of resource
 kinds it targets (empty = all resource kinds).
- **Value** — an allowed answer on that axis (`dev` / `staging` / `prod`). Each has an immutable
 `value` slug and a `label`. `assign` takes the **value slug**, so slugs must be discoverable —
 which is why `dimensions` prints them, not just a count.
- **Assignment** — a value pinned to one concrete resource, addressed by its **kind** and **id**.

 
Classification is **organizational metadata** — it does not enforce anything today. No policy,
permission check, provisioning step, or the [verify](/reference/glossary) gate reads these labels to
allow, deny, or route. See [Classification](/guides/classification#what-it-is-not--yet).

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: Addressing a resource: <kind> <id>
records.text:
`show`, `assign`, and `unassign` all target a resource by its **kind** (a snake-case record type) and
its **id** (a UUID). Those two are always yours to supply; the **dimension key** and the **value
slug** are not — omit them at a terminal and you are asked, from the org's own taxonomy. For example a project's default environment is `project_environment `.
The classifiable kinds mirror the console — projects, environments, clusters, cloud identities
(connectors), runners, members, roles, alert policies, alert channels, support cases. Audit-trail
records (alert *deliveries*, runner *usage sessions*) are intentionally not classifiable.

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: alethia classification dimensions
records.text:
List the org's dimensions and, for each, its allowed value slugs.

alethia classification dimensions

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: alias:
records.text:
alethia class dimensions

Columns: **Key**, **Label**, **Mode** (`single` `multi`), **Applies to** (the resource kinds, or
`all resources`), **Values** (the value slugs, comma-separated). In an interactive TTY this renders
as a navigable [TUI table](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs/blob/dev/docs/contributing/cli-tui.md); otherwise it prints a plain table. Add `-o json` for the raw
`ClassificationDimension` objects (including value `id`/`label` and per-dimension `description`).

KEY LABEL MODE APPLIES TO VALUES
environment Environment single project, project_environment dev, staging, prod
team Team multi all resources platform, payments, data
data-class Data classification single project_environment, cluster public, internal, restricted

Backing call: `GET /cli/classification/dimensions`.

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: alethia classification show
records.text:
Show the values currently assigned to one resource.

alethia classification show
alethia classification show project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000

Both tokens are optional at a terminal. Given neither, you are asked which **kind** — offered from
the kinds the org's own dimensions target, so it is not a string you have to have read out of
`dimensions` first — and then for the resource id. Scripted, pass both; `--no-input` with either
missing is refused, and the refusal names the two tokens rather than the prompt it could not open.

{/* fieldspec: alethia classification show */}

 Field What it is Set with 
 ------- ------------ ---------- 
 Resource kind The record type being labelled, e.g. project_environment `[kind]` 
 Resource id The UUID of the resource whose labels to read `[id]` 

Columns: **Dimension**, **Value** (both rendered as their human labels). Prints `Not classified.`
when the resource carries no values. Backing call:
`GET /cli/classification/assignments?kind= &id= `.

alethia classification show project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 -o json

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: alethia classification assign
records.text:
Pin a value to a resource.

alethia classification assign project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
alethia classification assign project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 environment prod

Given only the kind and the id at a terminal, you are asked which dimension — from the ones that
target that kind — and then which of **that dimension's** allowed values. Neither is a slug you
have to have read out of `dimensions` first.

Given all four, both slugs are checked against the org's taxonomy before anything is sent, and a
miss names the real keys or the real values rather than surfacing a 4xx.

{/* fieldspec: alethia classification assign */}

 Field What it is Set with 
 ------- ------------ ---------- 
 Resource kind The record type being labelled, e.g. project_environment ` ` 
 Resource id The UUID of the resource to label ` ` 
 Dimension Which axis to set, by its key; omit it to choose from the org's taxonomy `[dimension-key]` 
 Value The value slug to pin, from that dimension's allowed values `[value-slug]` 

For a **single**-valued dimension, assigning a new value **replaces** the current one; for a
**multi**-valued dimension, values accumulate. On

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: Label a project's default environment as prod, and tag two owning teams (multi dimension)
records.text:
alethia classification assign project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 environment prod
alethia classification assign project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 team platform
alethia classification assign project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 team payments

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: alethia classification unassign
records.text:
Clear a value from a resource (addressed by its **slug**, not the dimension key).

alethia classification unassign project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
alethia classification unassign project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 payments --yes

Clearing a value is destructive — policy that selects on it stops matching the resource — so it
asks before acting. In a pipeline `--yes` is **required**.

Omit the slug at a terminal and you choose from the values **the resource actually carries** — a
different source from `assign`'s, deliberately. `assign` chooses from everything that could be true
of the resource; `unassign` from what currently is, so you cannot clear a value it never had.

{/* fieldspec: alethia classification unassign */}

 Field What it is Set with 
 ------- ------------ ---------- 
 Resource kind The record type being labelled, e.g. project_environment ` ` 
 Resource id The UUID of the resource to clear a value from ` ` 
 Value The value slug to clear; omit it to choose from what the resource actually carries `[value-slug]` 

✓ Cleared payments from project_environment 8f3c1a2b-0000-4000-8000-000000000000

Backing call:
`DELETE /cli/cla

records.title: Classification Commands
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Classification (Console)](/guides/classification) — authoring dimensions/values, single vs multi,
 where the taxonomy applies, and usage insight.
- [Authentication](/reference/cli/authentication) — how the CLI obtains the token these commands use.
- [Command Reference](/reference/cli) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.text: Cloud Commands. Inspect the networking and regions Alethia discovered in a connected cloud account.

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.heading: Cloud Commands
records.text:
The `cloud` group reads the **inventory** Alethia discovered in a connected cloud account — the
networks (VPCs/VNets), subnets, and regions it swept.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `cloud inventory` calls
`/cli/cloud-identities/ /inventory` with your [CLI token](/reference/cli/authentication) and operates on
the **active organization** — the cloud identity must belong to it.

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.heading: alethia cloud inventory
records.text:
Show the discovered networking + regions for a connected cloud account.

bash

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.heading: Name the account by its provider
records.text:
alethia cloud inventory aws
alethia cloud inventory gcp -o json

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.heading: Or omit the argument for a picker over your connections
records.text:
alethia cloud inventory

 Argument Required Description 
 ---------- ---------- ------------- 
 `[provider]` No `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `alibaba`, or `hetzner`. Omit for a picker. A cloud-identity id is still accepted. 

 
**No id to copy.** This command used to take a bare ` ` — an opaque token
you had to copy out of another command's output before you could run it. Naming the provider
does the lookup for you, and omitting the argument shows a picker. An id a script already
holds keeps working, byte for byte: an id is a lookup key, so nothing here rewrites one.

Under `--no-input` there is no picker to show, so the argument is required and the refusal
says which providers are valid. If two accounts are connected for the same provider, the
command reports the ambiguity and lists their ids rather than guessing.
 

Renders a **Networks** table (network id, name, region, CIDR, default), a **Subnets** table
(subnet id, name, region, AZ, CIDR, public), and a **Regions** line. Add `-o json` for the full
inventory object; `-o csv` emits the networks rows. Prints `No cloud inventory discovered yet.`
when the account hasn't been swept. Backing call: `GET /cli/cloud-identities/ /inventory`.

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Connector Commands](/reference/cli/connector) — connect a cloud account.
- [Command Reference](/reference/cli) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.text: Cluster Commands. List the Kubernetes clusters your projects run on, and inspect one — status, sizing, cost, the kubeconfig command and ArgoCD access.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: Cluster Commands
records.text:
A cluster is what a project environment runs on. You do not create one here: provisioning an
environment creates it, and this group reads it back. The command is `alethia cluster` (singular)
with a `clusters` alias, so both forms work interchangeably.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. These commands call `/cli/clusters` with your
[CLI token](/reference/cli/authentication) and operate on the **active organization**, which you change with
`alethia org switch`. For one invocation, `alethia cluster list --org ` scopes the call to a
different organization instead — `--org` is a global flag, accepted on every command, and refused
with `403` if you are not a member of the organization you name.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: alethia cluster list
records.text:
List every cluster across your projects — one row per project environment.

alethia cluster list
alethia clusters list
alethia cluster list -o json

The command takes no input of its own; only the [global flags](/reference/cli) apply.

 Column Meaning 
 -------- --------- 
 Project The project and its environment — the same label `cluster get` titles its card with. 
 Cluster The cloud's name for the cluster, or `—` before it is provisioned. 
 Version The Kubernetes version. 
 Status A glyph and the status, with the status message appended when a cluster is degraded or failed. 
 ArgoCD `exposed` when a managed-ingress URL exists, `port-fwd` when access is by port-forward, `—` when the cluster is not provisioned yet. 
 Nodes Min / desired / max node count. 
 Region The cloud region. 
 Cost The estimated monthly cost, rendered exactly as the console's billing pages render it. 

Project Cluster Version Status ArgoCD Nodes Region Cost
api-backend (production) api-backend-production 1.30 ● active exposed 1/3/5 eu-west-1 $210.00/mo
data-pipeline (staging) data-pipeline-staging 1.29 ● active port-fwd 1/2/3 us-east4 $95.00/mo

At a terminal this is a navigable table; in a pipe, with `--no-i

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: alethia cluster get
records.text:
Show one cluster in full, including the command that gets you a kubeconfig and how to reach its ArgoCD.

alethia cluster get
alethia cluster get api-backend
alethia cluster get api-backend-production -o json

 Input Required Description 
 ------- ---------- ------------- 
 `[selector]` No — at a terminal Matches a project name, a cluster name, or a cluster id, case-insensitively. Falls back to a project-name substring. 

**Run it with no selector and the CLI asks which cluster**, listing every one you have with its
status. That is the whole reason the selector is optional: you never have to run `cluster list`
first and copy a name out of it.

The selector is required when a prompt could not work: with `--no-input`, with a piped stdin that
could never answer one, and with a redirected stdout that has no screen to draw one on. In each
case the command exits non-zero explaining what to pass. The last is the easy one to hit —
`alethia cluster get -o json > clusters.json` refuses rather than writing a form into your file.
A selector that matches **nothing** is an error too, not an empty screen —
`alethia cluster get typo echo missing` prints `missing`.

A selector that matches **more th

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: ArgoCD access
records.text:
ArgoCD is installed on every provisioned cluster. The **ArgoCD** row is its URL where a managed
ingress exists, and a note to port-forward where the cloud does not have one yet.

The admin password is **never stored by Alethia** — it would be plaintext in the control-plane
database — so the card prints the command that reads it from the cluster's own initial-admin
secret. It is a `kubectl` command, so get a kubeconfig first (the **Kubeconfig** row, above it),
then run:

kubectl -n argocd get secret argocd-initial-admin-secret -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' base64 -d

Where there is no managed ingress, reach the UI through a port-forward first:

kubectl -n argocd port-forward svc/argocd-server 8080:443

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: GitOps posture
records.text:
The **GitOps** row summarises the cluster's ArgoCD applications: how many are synced, how many are
healthy, and the short revision they are deployed at. It reads `failed at ` when the last
deploy failed, and `unknown (no snapshot yet)` when there is no trustworthy reading — which is a
different statement from "nothing is deployed", and deliberately not rendered as one.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: alethia cluster kubeconfig
records.text:
Get a short-lived kubeconfig for a cluster without a cloud login of your own. A runner in the
cluster's network mints the credential and seals it to a one-time key that this command makes.
Only this machine can open the result. For the task, with the tiers, lifetimes and revocation, see
[Get a kubeconfig for your cluster](/guides/get-a-kubeconfig).

alethia cluster kubeconfig
alethia cluster kubeconfig api-backend
alethia cluster kubeconfig api-backend --admin --ttl 4h
alethia cluster kubeconfig api-backend --output api-backend.kubeconfig
alethia cluster kubeconfig api-backend --static --output -
alethia cluster kubeconfig api-backend-production --no-input

 Input Required Default Description 
 ------- ---------- --------- ------------- 
 `[selector]` No — at a terminal The picker The same selector as `cluster get`: a project name, a cluster name or a cluster id. Omit it at a terminal and the CLI asks which cluster. 
 `--admin` No Off (read-only) Get the admin tier. Needs the `cluster:access_admin` permission, which owners and admins hold. Without it, the tier is read-only, which needs `cluster:access_readonly` (owners, admins and operators). 
 `--ttl` No `1h` The credential's life

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: Where the kubeconfig goes
records.text:
Flags Result 
 ------- -------- 
 None, or `--merge` The CLI merges the context `alethia- - ` into the first file in `$KUBECONFIG`, or into `~/.kube/config`, and makes it the current context. It replaces the cluster, user and context entries with that name, and keeps every other entry, unknown key and comment. It takes kubectl's ` .lock` lock while it writes, and follows a symlinked kubeconfig. 
 `--output FILE` The CLI writes a standalone kubeconfig to that file. 
 `--output -` The CLI writes the kubeconfig to stdout. This is the only way the credential goes to stdout. 

Every file the command writes gets mode `0600`, and the write is atomic. All other messages go to
stderr, so stdout is empty unless you pass `--output -`.

**The `--output` rules.** In this command `--output` takes a file path, not the global
`table`/`json`/`csv` format, and it has no `-o` short form. `--output table`, `--output json` and
`--output csv` are refused, so a habit cannot write a credential to a file called `json`. To write a
file with one of those names, pass `./json`. `--output` replaces the merge, so do not pass
`--merge` with it, not even as `--merge=false`: the two flags together are an error. Tur

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: Exec and static
records.text:
Shape Clouds What the kubeconfig holds 
 ------- -------- --------------------------- 
 Exec (the default) AWS, GCP, Azure No credential. It runs `alethia cluster token` with the cluster id, so `kubectl` gets a new token whenever one expires. The command also caches the token it just minted, so the first `kubectl` call does not wait for a runner. 
 Static (`--static`) All five, and always on Hetzner and Alibaba Cloud The credential itself: a bearer token, or a client certificate and key. It stops working at its expiry. 

The cluster list does not tell the CLI which cloud a cluster is on. So without `--static`, the CLI
asks for exec. If the cloud refuses (`422`), it asks again for static. A second `422` means the cloud
cannot mint either shape.

The exec kubeconfig pins the cluster's API server and certificate authority, and it never turns off
TLS verification. It needs the `alethia` command on the `PATH` of every machine that runs `kubectl`
with it.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: What the command prints

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: Exit codes and refusals
records.text:
The command exits `0` when it wrote the kubeconfig, and `1` for every error. It prints the error on
stderr after `Error:`. These are the refusals from the control plane, and what the CLI prints:

 Status Cause The CLI prints 
 -------- ------- ---------------- 
 `401` The session is not valid. Run `alethia login`. 
 `402` A usage limit of the organization's plan. The mint runs on a runner and uses runner minutes. The server's reason, and a pointer to `alethia usage`. 
 `403` Your role does not hold the tier's permission. Which roles can mint that tier. For `--admin`, a hint to drop it. 
 `404` No such cluster in the active organization. A pointer to `alethia org switch` and `--org`. 
 `409` The environment is a draft, is being destroyed, or has no successful deploy. The server's reason, and a pointer to `alethia project apply`. 
 `422` The cluster's cloud cannot mint a kubeconfig (it is not AWS, GCP, Azure, Alibaba Cloud or Hetzner, or it has no cloud identity). The server's reason. 
 `429` More than 20 requests in 10 minutes, per person, per organization. How long to wait, from the `Retry-After` header. 

After the request is accepted, the CLI polls until the mint is ready, failed

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: alethia cluster token
records.text:
Print a credential for `kubectl`. This is the exec plugin that the kubeconfig from
`alethia cluster kubeconfig` runs. You do not usually run it yourself.

alethia cluster token

 Input Required Default Description 
 ------- ---------- --------- ------------- 
 `[cluster-id]` No — at a terminal The picker The cluster id, a lowercase UUID as `cluster get` shows it. `kubectl` always passes it. Omit it at a terminal and the CLI asks which cluster, which is a way to check that your session can still mint. Without a terminal, it is required. 

The command takes no flags of its own. The global `--org` and `--token` flags apply.

**Stdout** carries one `client.authentication.k8s.io/v1` `ExecCredential` document and nothing
else: the token and its expiry. **Stderr** carries every error, after `alethia cluster token:`,
and `kubectl` shows that line. The command exits `0` when it printed a credential and `1`
otherwise. It never prompts: if your session expired, it fails and tells you to run
`alethia login`. It never prints the update notice.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: The cache
records.text:
The command keeps each credential in a cache until 60 seconds before the credential expires. So
only the first `kubectl` call in each credential's lifetime waits for a new mint.

 Property Value 
 ---------- ------- 
 Directory `alethia/kubecache` in the user configuration directory: `~/.config` on Linux (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS, `%AppData%` on Windows 
 Modes Directory `0700`, files `0600`. A directory that others can read is tightened. A cache file that is a symlink, is owned by another user, or that others can read is refused, not replaced. On Windows the user profile's access control applies instead. 
 Files per cluster The token and its expiry for each tier, the re-mint profile, and a lock file 
 Locking One lock per cluster. If several `kubectl` calls start on an empty cache, the first one mints and the others wait for it, so there is one mint.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: Re-minting
records.text:
When the cache has no fresh credential, the command mints a new one, in the exec shape, with the
profile that `alethia cluster kubeconfig` recorded: the tier, the TTL and the organization. It
uses that organization even if your active organization changed since, unless you pass `--org`.
A cluster with no profile, for example a kubeconfig copied from another machine, gets the
read-only tier with a 1-hour TTL in the active organization, never the admin tier.

Each mint checks your permission again. So a person whose role changes, or who leaves the
organization, stops getting tokens when the current one expires.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: Accessing a cluster with kubectl
records.text:
The **Kubeconfig** row is the command that writes a kubeconfig with **your own cloud CLI**, under
your own cloud login. Alethia does not issue a credential through this row: whether the command
works is your cloud account's decision. To get a kubeconfig through Alethia instead, use
[`alethia cluster kubeconfig`](#alethia-cluster-kubeconfig). In `-o json` output the same answer is the
`kubeconfig` object, with `command` and `note` fields.

Alethia builds the command from values the cluster's last successful deploy recorded, so it is
the same command the console's cluster card shows. Run it, then use `kubectl`:

 
 
 aws eks update-kubeconfig --name api-backend-production --region eu-west-1
 kubectl get nodes
 
 
 gcloud container clusters get-credentials data-pipeline-staging --region us-east4 --project acme-data-prod
 kubectl get nodes
 
 For a zonal cluster, one deployed to a zone such as `us-east4-a`, the command names the zone
 instead of the region.
 
 
 az aks get-credentials --resource-group rg-api-backend-production --name api-backend-production
 kubectl get nodes
 
 
 Alethia does not record the ACK cluster ID yet, and ACK's kubeconfig API needs it. The
 **Kubeconfig** row

records.title: Configuration
records.text: Configuration. CLI configuration files, environment variables, and credential storage.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Configuration
records.text:
alethia stores configuration and credentials under the OS user-config directory (`~/.config/alethia`
on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/alethia` on macOS — the location follows Go's
`os.UserConfigDir`). Inspect the resolved values and on-disk paths at any time with
[`alethia config`](#alethia-config).

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: File Locations
records.text:
File Purpose 
 ------ --------- 
 `~/.config/alethia/credentials.json` CLI authentication tokens (access + refresh JWT) 
 `~/.config/alethia/config.json` Active organization context (id, name, slug)

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: credentials.json
records.text:
Created by `alethia login`. Contains JWT tokens for API authentication:

{
 "access_token": "eyJ...",
 "refresh_token": "eyJ...",
 "user_email": "you@example.com"
}

The access token is refreshed automatically before each API call if expired. See [Authentication](/reference/cli/authentication).

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: config.json
records.text:
Created/updated by `alethia org switch`. Records the active organization, which is sent as the
`X-Alethia-Org` header on every request:

{
 "active_org_id": "org_123",
 "active_org_name": "Acme",
 "active_org_slug": "acme"
}

Clear it with `alethia config clear-context`.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: alethia config
records.text:
Show the resolved CLI configuration: the control-plane URL (`ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN`), the active
organization context, and the on-disk paths of the credentials and config files.

alethia config

Field Value
web origin https://app.alethialabs.io (config)
active org Acme
active org id org_123
credentials /Users/you/Library/Application Support/alethia/credentials.json
config /Users/you/Library/Application Support/alethia/config.json

`alethia config clear-context` clears the active organization context. `alethia config -o json`
emits the same values as a JSON object.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Config keys
records.text:
These are the keys `alethia config get` reads. `alethia config set` writes the ones marked
`config set`; a key set anywhere else says which command owns it, because a value you can read and
cannot write needs to tell you what does write it.

{/* configkeys */}

 Key What it is How to set it 
 --- --- --- 
 `web-origin` The control-plane URL the CLI talks to (hosted, self-hosted or dev). `config set` 
 `active-org` The organization every request is scoped to, sent as X-Alethia-Org. `alethia org switch` 

`active-org` is deliberately read-only. Setting it by name would have to resolve that name to an id
and a slug — which is a server round-trip, and that round-trip is `alethia org switch`. A
`config set active-org` that wrote only the name would leave the id stale and scope every subsequent
request to the *previous* organization.

The underscore spellings (`web_origin`, `active_org`) are accepted too, because that is how the keys
appear in `config.json` and people type what they have read.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: alethia config set
records.text:
alethia config set # pick the key, edit the current value
alethia config set web-origin https://alethia.internal.example.com # the same, unattended

Run with no arguments on a terminal, `config set` asks for both:

{/* fieldspec: alethia config set */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Config key Which value to change `[key]` 
 Value The new value; the form describes it with the chosen key's own summary `[value]` 

The value field is pre-filled with the **stored** value, so the form is an edit rather than a
re-type, and it is validated by the same rule `config set` applies — a value the form accepts is
never refused a moment later. It shows what is stored rather than what is in effect, because that
is what the write replaces: if `ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN` is set, the form says so and still seeds the
file's value, so pressing Enter cannot overwrite it with the environment's.

With `--no-input` both arguments are required; the command fails rather than guessing.

 
`ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN` **outranks** the config file. If it is set to a different URL,
`alethia config set web-origin` says so after saving, because otherwise the write appears to succeed
and every subsequent

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: alethia config export
records.text:
Export an environment's **design document** — the same nested shape the console design form holds,
and the one [`alethia project design apply`](/reference/cli/project) accepts. By default the content is
written to stdout; pass `--out` to write it to a file, or `-o json` to get the export envelope
(content + filename + format).

bash

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Print the design document to stdout
records.text: alethia config export my-project

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Round-trip it: export, edit, apply
records.text:
alethia config export my-project --out my-project.json
alethia project design apply -p my-project -f my-project.json --dry-run
alethia project design apply -p my-project -f my-project.json

 Flag Default Description 
 ------ --------- ------------- 
 `--format` `json` The content format. `json` is the only supported value. 
 `--out` _(stdout)_ Write the content to this file instead of stdout. 

The project name is optional — omit it in an interactive terminal to pick one from a list. Backing
call: `GET /cli/configurations/by-project-name/ /export`.

 
 **Before 0.5.x this command did not work at all.** The route it calls did not exist, so every
 invocation 404'd, and its default `--format legacy-yaml` named a format nothing in the product has
 ever produced. If you pinned `--format legacy-yaml`, drop it or pass `json`; the server now refuses
 that value by name rather than returning JSON labelled as YAML.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Runner Credentials
records.text:
The `alethia` CLI does not store Runner credentials. A self-operated Runner is a
separate binary configured entirely through environment variables — register the
Runner in the console (or via the API) to obtain a `runner_id` / `runner_token`,
then set `ALETHIA_RUNNER_ID` and `ALETHIA_RUNNER_TOKEN` on the host. See
[Self-Operated Runners](/guides/runners/self-operated) for the full env contract.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Environment Variables
records.text:
Variable Default Purpose 
 ---------- --------- --------- 
 `ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN` `https://alethialabs.io` (compiled-in default) Override the Alethia API base URL 
 `ALETHIA_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` unset Disable the daily interactive new-release notice 

These are the CLI configuration environment variables. Runner processes use a separate runtime
environment documented with the runner deployment method.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Global Flags
records.text:
Four persistent flags are available on every command:

 Flag Default Description 
 ------ --------- ------------- 
 `-o, --output ` `table` Output format. `json`/`csv` print static, machine-readable output, and never open an interactive table. 
 `--no-input` off Disable interactive prompts; fail instead of prompting. Auto-enabled when stdin is not a terminal. A form is refused separately when the stream it would draw on is redirected, so `alethia … 2> log` still renders the rich table. 
 `--token ` unset Service-account token for non-interactive use. Prefer the `ALETHIA_TOKEN` environment variable in CI: a flag value lands in the process table and in shell history. 
 `--org ` the active org Organization to act in for this invocation, instead of the active one. Sent as the `X-Alethia-Org` header on every request, and used as the org in the request path of `members` and `teams`. It selects a scope rather than granting one: the control plane refuses it with `403` when you are not a member of that organization. Under a service token it must name the token's OWN organization — a different one is refused with `403`, never quietly ignored, so a pipeline cannot believe it is acting on one

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Control-Plane URL Resolution
records.text:
The control-plane URL resolves in precedence order: the `ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN` environment
variable, then the persisted config (`alethia config set web-origin `), then a compiled-in
default (`https://alethialabs.io`). The hosted default is a constant baked into the binary, so the
production build needs no configuration (GoReleaser's `ldflags` inject only the CLI version, not the
URL). For development or a self-hosted control plane, override it with the environment variable:

alethia login # authenticates against local server

records.title: Connector Commands
records.text: Connector Commands. Connect AWS, GCP, Azure, Alibaba and Hetzner cloud accounts to Alethia entirely from the terminal.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connector Commands
records.text:
The `connector` command group connects your cloud accounts to Alethia so the platform can
provision infrastructure into them. It drives the **same connection flow as the web console's
[Connectors](/guides/connectors) page**, but end-to-end from the CLI — there is no need to
open a browser for the default flows.

 
Each connection is a **[cloud identity](/reference/glossary)** — the credential anchor a
[project](/reference/glossary) links to (`cloud_identity_id`). "Connector" is the catalog of provider
*types*; the record `alethia connector` creates for your account is a cloud identity. A project
points at exactly one. Every cloud-identity query is filtered by provider, so accounts never leak
across providers.
 

Every connection to a cloud that supports it uses **short-lived, keyless credentials** — AWS
cross-account roles, GCP Workload Identity Federation, Azure federated identity, Alibaba RAM
`AssumeRoleWithOIDC`. No access keys or client secrets are created or stored for any of them.

**Hetzner is the single exception, and the exception is the cloud's.** Hetzner Cloud exposes no OIDC
provider and no role-assumption API, so it authenticates with a scoped API token — see
[`alethia

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: How It Works
records.text:
Each `connector` subcommand runs the same three-stage pipeline, verified server-side:

 aws · gcp · azure · alibaba · hetzner] --> B[Init pending cloud identity]
 B --> C[Run provider setup IAM OIDC role · WIF pool · federated cred · RAM OIDC · API token]
 C --> D[Submit captured credentials]
 D --> E[Server-side verify auth + permission probe]
 E --> F{Verdict}
 F --> G[Connected]
 F --> H[Degraded]
 F --> I[Disconnected]
`} />

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Initialize
records.text: The CLI creates (or reuses) a pending cloud identity for the provider.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Run provider setup
records.text:
The CLI drives the provider's own tooling to create the resources Alethia needs (an IAM OIDC provider +
role, a workload identity pool, or an app registration) and captures the resulting credential
material.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Submit & verify
records.text:
The captured credentials are sent to Alethia, which verifies them **instantly, server-side** — an
auth + provisioning-permission probe (no runner). The identity is marked `Connected`, `Degraded`, or
`Disconnected` and is ready to provision into. Existing resources are discovered separately by the
server-side [asset inventory](/guides/connectors/health-and-inventory).

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Prerequisites
records.text:
- You must be authenticated: run [`alethia login`](/reference/cli/authentication) first.
- For the **default** flows, the matching provider CLI must be installed and authenticated
 locally:
 - GCP → `gcloud` (used to drive Google Cloud Shell)
 - AWS → `aws`
 - Azure → `az`
 - Alibaba → `aliyun`
 - Hetzner → **none**; it is a token, so there is nothing to install
- The `--manual` flows require **none** of the above — you run a one-liner in the provider's
 browser shell and paste the result back.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Execution Models
records.text:
Provider Default Why 
 ---------- --------- ----- 
 GCP Runs the installer inside your **Google Cloud Shell** (via local `gcloud`) Cloud Shell is already authenticated to your GCP org and has every tool preinstalled 
 AWS Deploys CloudFormation with the **local `aws` CLI** AWS CloudShell is browser-only — there is no remote-exec CLI 
 Azure Runs the setup script with the **local `az` CLI** Azure Cloud Shell is browser-only — there is no remote-exec CLI 
 Alibaba Runs the setup script with the **local `aliyun` CLI** Alibaba Cloud Shell is browser-only — there is no remote-exec CLI (as with AWS and Azure) 
 Hetzner Prompts for a scoped **API token** Hetzner Cloud has no OIDC or role assumption, so there is nothing to set up — only a credential to capture 

The four keyless providers support `--manual`, which prints a link + command to run in the browser
shell and prompts you to paste the result — use it when you cannot or prefer not to install the local
CLI. Alibaba additionally supports `--terraform`, which writes an OpenTofu module you apply yourself
(see [`alethia connector alibaba`](#alethia-connector-alibaba)).

Hetzner needs no such flow: there is no installer, only the token i

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Scripting: flags are a complete contract
records.text:
Everything the interactive flows can ask for, a flag can set — so every `connector` command
works under `--no-input`, in CI, with no cloud CLI installed and no terminal to prompt on.
That is what the `--role-arn`, `--wif-config`, `--tenant-id` and `--client-id` flags are for:
they are the flag form of the `--manual` pastes, for a role or managed identity you have
already created.

alethia connector aws --no-input \
 --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AlethiaProvisionerRole

alethia connector gcp --no-input --project my-gcp-project --wif-config ./wif.json

alethia connector azure --no-input \
 --subscription 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 \
 --tenant-id 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 \
 --client-id 22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222

alethia connector alibaba --no-input \
 --role-arn acs:ram::123456789012:role/AlethiaProvisioner

echo "$HCLOUD_TOKEN" alethia connector hetzner --no-input --token-stdin

Leave a required field out under `--no-input` and the command exits non-zero **naming the
flag** that would have supplied it, rather than failing at a prompt it cannot open.

Each command takes **one** setup mode. Submitting something you already have and asking fo

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector gcp
records.text:
Connect a Google Cloud project using Workload Identity Federation.

alethia connector gcp --project my-gcp-project

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project` No GCP project ID. Prompted interactively if omitted. 
 `--wif-config` No Path to a WIF credential config JSON you already have, or `-` to read it from stdin. The flag form of the `--manual` paste. 
 `--manual` No Run the installer in the browser Cloud Shell and paste the result instead of using local `gcloud`. 

By default, the CLI runs an installer **inside your Google Cloud Shell**. Cloud Shell is
authenticated as you, so the provisioner service account and a workload identity pool that trusts
Alethia are created directly in your project — and the CLI captures the generated WIF credential
config automatically. No service account keys are ever created.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Enter the project
records.text: Provide `--project`, or type it at the prompt.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Cloud Shell setup
records.text:
The CLI invokes `gcloud cloud-shell ssh`, pushes the installer, and runs it. The first run can take
a minute while Cloud Shell provisions.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connection test
records.text:
The captured WIF config is submitted, verified instantly server-side, and the identity is marked Connected (or Degraded/Disconnected).

 

Sample run:

◆ Project ── ◇ Cloud Shell setup ── ◇ Connection test

Running installer via gcloud Cloud Shell (the first run can take a minute)...
✔ Cloud Shell ready.
✔ Installer running in Cloud Shell.
...
--- START CONFIG (copy everything below until END CONFIG) ---
{ ...WIF credential config... }
--- END CONFIG ---

✓ Verifying connection (server-side)...
✓ Connected

✓ GCP project "my-gcp-project" connected

 
If `gcloud` is not logged in, Cloud Shell cannot authenticate non-interactively and you will see a
reauth error. Run `gcloud auth login`, then retry — or use `alethia connector gcp --manual`.

✗ gcloud is not authenticated
Run this, then retry:

 gcloud auth login

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Manual GCP setup
records.text:
With `--manual`, the CLI prints a Cloud Shell link and a command, then waits for you to paste the
WIF config:

alethia connector gcp --project my-gcp-project --manual

1. Open [Google Cloud Shell](https://shell.cloud.google.com/cloudshell/open?shellonly=true&show=terminal).
2. Run the printed command:
 curl -sO https://alethia-connector-assets.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/alethia-gcp-setup.sh \
 && bash alethia-gcp-setup.sh my-gcp-project
 3. Paste everything between `--- START CONFIG ---` and `--- END CONFIG ---` at the prompt.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector aws
records.text:
Connect an AWS account using a keyless, issuer-direct IAM role (an IAM OIDC provider trusting the Alethia
issuer — no access keys, no external id).

alethia connector aws

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--region` No AWS region for the CloudFormation stack. 
 `--role-name` No Name for the IAM role. Defaults to `AlethiaProvisionerRole`. 
 `--role-arn` No ARN of a role you already created. Submits it instead of prompting — the flag form of the `--manual` paste. 
 `--manual` No Deploy from the AWS console and paste the role ARN instead of using local `aws`. 
 `--script` No Use the `aws`-CLI setup script instead of the CloudFormation stack. 

 
 

The CLI deploys the bundled CloudFormation template with your local `aws` credentials, then reads
the created role ARN from the stack outputs and submits it automatically.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Initialize
records.text: Alethia creates a pending cloud identity for the connection.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Create the IAM role
records.text:
The CLI runs `aws cloudformation deploy` (stack `AlethiaConnect`), creating an IAM OIDC provider for the
Alethia issuer + a role that trusts it via `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` (pinned to the fixed audience and
subject).

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connection test
records.text:
The role ARN is submitted, the connection is verified instantly server-side, and the identity is marked Connected (or Degraded/Disconnected).

 

alethia connector aws --region eu-west-1

 
 

With `--manual`, the CLI prints a CloudFormation **quick-create** link pre-filled with the Alethia issuer
URL and prompts for the resulting role ARN:

alethia connector aws --manual

1. Open the printed quick-create link (it pre-fills the template and issuer URL).
2. Acknowledge the IAM capabilities checkbox and create the stack.
3. Copy the `RoleArn` from the stack **Outputs** tab and paste it at the prompt:
 ? Role ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AlethiaProvisionerRole

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector azure
records.text:
Connect an Azure subscription using federated identity (no client secret).

alethia connector azure

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--subscription` No Azure subscription ID. Prompted interactively if omitted. 
 `--tenant-id` No Tenant ID of a managed identity you already created. Requires `--client-id`. 
 `--client-id` No Client (application) ID of that managed identity. Requires `--tenant-id`. 
 `--manual` No Run setup in Azure Cloud Shell and paste the result instead of using local `az`. 

 
 

The CLI runs the setup script with your local `az` login. It creates a user-assigned managed
identity (a plain ARM resource — no app registration, no client secret), a federated credential
trusting Alethia's OIDC issuer, and a least-privilege role assignment, then captures the tenant,
client, and subscription IDs automatically.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Enter the subscription
records.text: Provide `--subscription`, or type it at the prompt.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Create the managed identity
records.text:
The CLI runs the setup script via `az`, creating the managed identity, federated credential, and
role assignment.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connection test
records.text:
The captured IDs are submitted, the connection is verified instantly server-side, and the identity is marked Connected (or Degraded/Disconnected).

 

 
 

With `--manual`, the CLI prints a command to run in Azure Cloud Shell and prompts for the three
IDs the script outputs:

alethia connector azure --manual

1. Open [Azure Cloud Shell](https://shell.azure.com).
2. Run the printed command. It already carries your subscription ID:
 curl -sO https://alethia-connector-assets.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/alethia-azure-setup.sh \
 && bash alethia-azure-setup.sh 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
 3. Paste the **Tenant ID**, **Client ID**, and **Subscription ID** it prints at the prompts.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector alibaba
records.text:
Connect an Alibaba Cloud account using keyless `AssumeRoleWithOIDC`. By default the CLI runs a setup
script with your local `aliyun` CLI: it creates a RAM OIDC provider trusting the Alethia issuer plus
a RAM role, and captures the resulting role ARN automatically. Use `--manual` to run the same script
in the Alibaba Cloud Shell, or `--terraform` to apply an OpenTofu module instead. Alethia stores
nothing but the role ARN — no AccessKey.

alethia connector alibaba

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--region` No Alibaba region for the RAM provider. Defaults to `cn-hangzhou`. 
 `--role-arn` No ARN of a RAM role you already created. Submits it instead of prompting — the flag form of the `--manual` paste. 
 `--manual` No Run the setup script in the Alibaba Cloud Shell and paste the role ARN. 
 `--terraform` No Apply the OpenTofu module instead of running the setup script. 
 `--dir` No Directory to write the OpenTofu module into (with `--terraform`). Defaults to `./alethia-alibaba-connector`.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Initialize
records.text: Alethia creates a pending [cloud identity](/reference/glossary) for the connection.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Create the RAM role
records.text:
The CLI runs the setup script with your local `aliyun` CLI, creating a RAM OIDC provider trusting the
Alethia issuer (` /api/oidc`) plus a RAM role, and captures the role ARN from its
output. With `--manual`, run the same script in the Alibaba Cloud Shell and paste the ARN back.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connection test
records.text:
The role ARN is submitted, verified instantly server-side, and the identity is marked Connected (or
Degraded/Disconnected). Alethia stores nothing but the role ARN — no AccessKey.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: OpenTofu module (--terraform)
records.text:
With `--terraform`, the CLI writes `main.tf` into the target directory (`--dir`) instead of running
the setup script. It provisions the same RAM OIDC provider + role. Authenticate to Alibaba (the
`aliyun` CLI, or `ALICLOUD_ACCESS_KEY` / `ALICLOUD_SECRET_KEY`), apply it, then paste the `role_arn`
output at the prompt:

cd alethia-alibaba-connector
tofu init
tofu apply -var "region=cn-hangzhou" -var "alethia_issuer_url=https://alethialabs.io/api/oidc"

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector hetzner
records.text:
Connect a Hetzner Cloud account with a scoped API token.

bash

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Prompted, masked — the token never reaches your shell history
records.text: alethia connector hetzner

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: From a pipe, for scripts and CI
records.text: echo "$HCLOUD_TOKEN" alethia connector hetzner --token-stdin

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: With Object Storage credentials, if this project declares storage buckets
records.text:
alethia connector hetzner --token-stdin \
 --s3-access-key "$HETZNER_S3_ACCESS_KEY" --s3-secret-key "$HETZNER_S3_SECRET_KEY"

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--token-stdin` No Read the API token from stdin. Preferred for scripts. 
 `--token` No Pass the token inline. Convenient, but it lands in your shell history and the process list. 
 `--s3-access-key` No Hetzner Object Storage access key. Only needed for storage buckets, and only together with `--s3-secret-key`. 
 `--s3-secret-key` No Hetzner Object Storage secret key. Only together with `--s3-access-key`. 

The Object Storage keys are a **pair**: give both or neither. Half a pair is refused rather
than stored, because an access key with no secret is a credential that cannot work and whose
failure only shows up later, as a bucket that will not provision. On a terminal the command
offers the pair after the token prompt, so you never have to know the flag names.

Create the token in the Hetzner Cloud Console, under the **project** rather than the account:
**Security → API tokens → Generate API token**, with **Read & Write**. Object Storage uses a
separate pair under **Security → S3 credentials**.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector list
records.text:
List all connected (verified) cloud accounts.

alethia connector list

Output:

PROVIDER ACCOUNT CONNECTED
AWS AWS (123456789012) 2 hours ago
GCP GCP (my-gcp-project) 5 days ago
AZURE Azure (3f9a1c2b-...) 5 days ago

The table is interactive — sort and navigate with the keyboard (see [TUI Components](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs/blob/dev/docs/contributing/cli-tui.md)).

**PROVIDER** is upper-cased and **CONNECTED** is an age for a person reading the column. Under
`-o csv` a script gets the values instead: the provider is the lower-case wire value — the same
string `alethia connector aws` takes and `-o json` marshals — and **CONNECTED** is the RFC3339
stamp, which sorts and parses.
Add `-o json` for the full records, including each connection's `id`.

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 _(none)_ — `connector list` takes no input of its own.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector remove
records.text:
Disconnect a cloud account.

alethia connector remove gcp

If you omit the provider, the CLI shows a picker of connected accounts. Under `--no-input`
there is no picker to show, so the provider argument is required and the refusal says so.

 Argument Required Description 
 ---------- ---------- ------------- 
 `[provider]` No `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `alibaba`, or `hetzner`. Omit for a picker. 

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `-y`, `--yes` No Skip the confirmation prompt. Required with `--no-input`. 

 
Disconnecting resets the identity to a pending state and **orphans any projects** that referenced it
(their `cloud_identity_id` is cleared). It does not destroy already-provisioned cloud resources —
run [`alethia project destroy`](/reference/cli/plan-and-apply) first to tear those down. You can
reconnect the same provider later.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Troubleshooting
records.text:
Symptom Cause & fix 
 --------- ------------- 
 `gcloud is not authenticated` / reauth error Cloud Shell cannot prompt non-interactively. Run `gcloud auth login`, then retry — or use `--manual`. 
 `gcloud CLI not found on PATH` Install the [Google Cloud CLI](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install), or use `--manual`. 
 `aws CLI not found on PATH` / `az CLI not found on PATH` Install the provider CLI, or use `--manual` to set the connection up from the browser. 
 `could not find WIF config in installer output` The Cloud Shell installer did not finish. Re-run, or use `--manual` and paste the config yourself. 
 `Captured WIF config is not valid JSON` The pasted block was truncated. Copy everything between `--- START CONFIG ---` and `--- END CONFIG ---`. 
 Connection test fails Alethia could not assume the credentials. Confirm the role trust policy pins the Alethia issuer + sub/aud (AWS), the workload identity binding (GCP), or the federated credential + least-privilege role (Azure). The verify runs inline server-side and returns the reason with the result — re-run the connector command to see it. 
 `Invalid format. Expected: arn:aws:iam::…` The pasted role ARN is malformed — copy t

records.title: Cost Commands
records.text: Cost Commands. Inspect a project environment's infrastructure cost — the latest Infracost breakdown a plan captured.

records.title: Cost Commands
records.heading: Cost Commands
records.text:
The `cost` group reads a project environment's **infrastructure cost**. Every PLAN runs Infracost
over the OpenTofu plan and records the priced breakdown per environment; this command shows the
latest one.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `cost show` calls `/cli/projects/ /cost` with
your [CLI token](/reference/cli/authentication) and operates on the **active organization**
(`alethia org switch`). Pass `--org ` to scope a single invocation to a different organization —
it is refused with `403` if you are not a member of it.

records.title: Cost Commands
records.heading: alethia cost show
records.text:
Show the latest cost for a project environment.

alethia cost show # picks the project interactively (terminal, table output)
alethia cost show --project my-project
alethia cost show -p my-project -e staging
alethia cost show -p my-project -o json

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project`, `-p` No Project name or id. Omit on a TTY for the interactive project picker. 
 `--env`, `-e` No Environment name, stage, or id. Omit to use the project's default environment. 

Run without `--project` on a terminal and the CLI shows the same project picker as `project plan`
and `project apply`. The flag is the complete contract — it can set anything the picker can ask —
so `--no-input` never needs a terminal. Under `--no-input` an omitted project is refused with a
message that names `--project`.

The picker appears **only** for the default table output on a terminal. `-o json`, `-o csv`,
`--no-input` and a redirected stdout all refuse an omitted `--project` with that same message,
because the picker draws on stdout and would otherwise put a spinner and a menu in the file you
redirected the document into.

The command prints a one-line headline — the total monthl

records.title: Cost Commands
records.heading: How the amounts are written
records.text:
Every amount — the headline and each row — is rendered by the same shared formatter the console
uses, so a cost you read in the terminal and the same cost on the project canvas cannot disagree.

- **One currency, once.** The amount is written in the environment's own currency: `€123.45/mo` for
 a euro environment, never a dollar sign with the code `EUR` appended. A currency the formatter has
 no symbol for is written with its ISO code instead — `123.45 HUF/mo` — and never with a guessed
 symbol.
- **Cents are never dropped.** Rows and headline round identically, so the column adds up to the
 total.
- **`captured` is a date, not a wire timestamp** — `1 Jan 2026, 00:00`, in UTC, so the same record
 reads the same on every machine.

All of that is the **table** render, which is written for a person. Use `-o json` when a script
needs the raw number: `total_monthly` and each `monthly_cost` are plain numbers, and `currency` is
the ISO code.

records.title: Drift Commands
records.text: Drift Commands. Inspect a project's day-2 drift posture — which managed resources have diverged from their provisioned state.

records.title: Drift Commands
records.heading: Drift Commands
records.text:
The `drift` group reads the **day-2 drift posture** of a project — the "keep proving it" half of
Alethia. A `DETECT_DRIFT` job runs a refresh-only plan and records which managed resources have
diverged from their provisioned state; this command shows the latest result.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `drift show` calls `/cli/projects/PROJECT/drift`
with your [CLI token](/reference/cli/authentication) and operates on the **active organization**
(switch it with `alethia org switch`). Pass the global `--org ` to scope a single invocation to
a different organization — it is refused with `403` if you are not a member of it.

records.title: Drift Commands
records.heading: alethia drift show
records.text:
Show the latest drift posture for a project, optionally scoped to one environment.

alethia drift show --project my-project
alethia drift show -p my-project -e production
alethia drift show -p my-project -o json

{/* fieldspec: alethia drift */}

 Field What it is How to set it 
 --- --- --- 
 Project The project, by name or id; omit it on a terminal and you are asked `--project` 
 Environment The environment, by name, stage or id; empty means every environment in the project `--env` 

`--project` has the short form `-p` and `--env` has `-e`. On a terminal, omitting `--project` opens
the project picker; with `--no-input`, with `-o json`, or with the output redirected to a file, it
is required — a form drawn into a redirected stream would corrupt the document you are piping.

The command prints a one-line headline — **in sync**, **N resource(s) drifted**, or **not
evaluated** when no drift scan has ever run (an honest "not proven", never a false in-sync) —
followed by a table of the drifted resources:

Drift [production]: 2 resource(s) drifted (scanned 1 Jan 2026, 00:00)
Address Type Change
aws_db_instance.main aws_db_instance modified
aws_s3_bucket.logs aws_s3_bucket deleted

Add `

records.title: IaC Commands
records.text: IaC Commands. Attach, scan, show and detach the BYO Terraform/OpenTofu source on a project environment.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: IaC Commands
records.text:
The `iac` group manages the **BYO Terraform/OpenTofu source** attached to an environment — your own
IaC module, pulled from a connected git repo, that Alethia applies for that environment.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. These commands call `/cli/projects/PROJECT/byo-iac`
with your [CLI token](/reference/cli/authentication) and operate on the **active organization**.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: Common flags
records.text:
Every command in the group takes the same two selectors. They are registered on the group, so they
work in any position.

{/* fieldspec: alethia iac */}

 Field What it is How to set it 
 --- --- --- 
 Project The project, by name or id; omit it on a terminal and you are asked `--project` 
 Environment The environment, by name, stage or id; empty means the project's default `--env` 

`--project` has the short form `-p` and `--env` has `-e`. On a terminal, omitting `--project` opens
the project picker; with `--no-input`, with `-o json`, or with the output redirected to a file, it
is required — a form drawn into a redirected stream would corrupt the document you are piping.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: alethia iac show
records.text:
Show the BYO IaC source attached to a project environment.

alethia iac show --project my-project
alethia iac show -p my-project -e staging
alethia iac show -p my-project -o json

Renders a field/value card: **name**, **repo**, **path**, **ref**, **enabled**, **scan** (the
IaC-safety scan lifecycle), **pinned commit** (what a deploy will apply), **deployed commit** (what
the last deploy applied), **status**. Prints `No BYO IaC source attached.` when none is configured.
Add `-o json` for the full source object — the Elench scan report itself is console-only. Backing
call: `GET /cli/projects/PROJECT/byo-iac`.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: alethia iac attach
records.text:
Attach a git repository holding your own Terraform/OpenTofu to one environment.

alethia iac attach -p shop -e dev --repo https://github.com/acme/infra --path iac/drift/aws --ref main --var region=eu-west-1

{/* fieldspec: alethia iac attach */}

 Field What it is How to set it 
 --- --- --- 
 Repository The git repository holding your Terraform/OpenTofu `--repo` 
 Module path Where the module sits inside the repository; empty is the repository root `--path` 
 Git ref The branch, tag or commit to apply; empty tracks the repository's default branch `--ref` 
 Variable One scalar tfvar key=value, repeatable, and never a place for a secret `--var`

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: The interactive path
records.text:
Run `alethia iac attach` on a terminal with nothing else and it asks for each field it was not
given. A flag you did pass is never questioned again.

The **repository is chosen, not typed**: the form asks which connected provider to look in, then
offers the repositories Alethia can already see, with `Type a URL instead…` at the bottom of the
list. If no provider is connected, or the listing fails, the question falls back to a plain typed
line rather than refusing the attach.

The run finishes by printing the flags that would have produced the same result.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: With --no-input
records.text:
Nothing is asked, and `--repo` is required. Every field above has a flag, so any attach the form can
perform, a script can perform.

 
 **A private repository needs no credential flag.** The runner fetches a short-lived token at job
 time from your linked GitHub or GitLab account, scoped to the repositories this project declares,
 and refreshed per job — so nothing is stored against the source. Link that account once in the
 console and private repositories work.
 

An environment holds **at most one** source, so re-attaching replaces it.

 
 `--var` takes **scalars only** — string, number or bool. The server refuses a nested object or an
 array, and tfvars are never a place for a secret. Use the platform's secret handling for anything
 sensitive.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: alethia iac scan
records.text:
alethia iac scan -p shop -e dev

An attached source is **not deployable until scanned**: the scan reads the module's variables and
records the verdict the plan-time gate reads. The scan is asynchronous: the queued job id is
printed, and `alethia jobs logs --latest --follow` tails it without repeating that id back.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: alethia iac detach
records.text:
alethia iac detach -p shop -e dev --yes

 
 Detaching stops Alethia managing what the source created. Resources it applied are **not
 destroyed** — run a destroy first if that is what you want. The command confirms first and names
 the environment; with `--no-input`, or when stdin is not a terminal, `--yes` is required and the
 command fails without it rather than cancelling quietly.
 

 
 These commands need `ALETHIA_BYO_IAC_ENABLED=true` on the instance, and attaching is refused with
 **409** when the environment already holds template-provisioned state — a conflict with reality that
 no retry will clear.

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.text: Identity & Global Options. whoami, config, output formats, the --no-input flag, and utility commands (version, open, completion).

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: Identity & Global Options
records.text:
This page covers the top-level commands that tell you **who you are** and **how the CLI is
configured**, plus the global flags and utility commands available everywhere.

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: alethia whoami
records.text:
Show who you are signed in as: the authenticated user, the active organization, your role in it, the
org's plan, and its default runner.

alethia whoami

Field Value
User you@example.com
Name Ada Lovelace
Organization Acme
Slug acme
Role owner
Plan pro
Default runner acme-eu-west-1

Use `--output json` for scripting:

alethia whoami -o json jq '.active_org.slug'

If no organization is active, the `Organization` row shows a dash — set one with
[`alethia org switch`](/reference/cli/organizations#alethia-org-switch).

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: alethia config
records.text:
Show the resolved CLI configuration: the control-plane URL (`ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN`), the active
organization context, and the on-disk paths of the credentials and config files.

alethia config

`alethia config clear-context` clears the active organization. See
[Configuration](/reference/cli/configuration#alethia-config) for the full output and file layout.

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: Output Formats
records.text:
Every command accepts a global output flag:

-o, --output (default: table)

 Format Behavior 
 -------- ---------- 
 `table` Human-readable. On a TTY, list/get commands render an **interactive** table (sort, navigate, quit). 
 `json` Static, machine-readable JSON — ideal for piping into `jq`. 
 `csv` Static comma-separated rows — ideal for spreadsheets and `cut`/`awk`. 

bash

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: Pipe JSON into jq
records.text: alethia project list -o json jq '.[].name'

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: Export a CSV of jobs
records.text:
alethia jobs list -o csv > jobs.csv

When output is **not** `table` (or stdout is piped / `--no-input` is set), list/get commands print
static output instead of the interactive table — so they're safe to use in scripts and CI.

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: The --no-input Flag
records.text:
--no-input Disable interactive prompts (fail instead of prompting).

Interactive selectors and confirmation prompts are disabled with `--no-input`. It is **auto-enabled
when stdin is not a TTY** (a pipe, CI, etc.), so the CLI never hangs waiting for input that can't
come. With prompting disabled, supply required values explicitly (`--project-id`, `--runner-id`, an
org argument, …) or the command fails with a clear error. See [TUI Components](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs/blob/dev/docs/contributing/cli-tui.md).

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: alethia version
records.text:
Print the CLI version and check the control plane for the latest available release. If the network
is unavailable, the command falls back to the last successful daily check.

alethia version

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: alethia update
records.text:
Update the CLI through its detected installation channel. Homebrew and Scoop remain responsible for
their installations; writable standalone binaries are downloaded and checksum-verified directly.
Linux packages, Docker images, and non-writable installations receive an exact manual command.

alethia update

The command does not elevate privileges. See [Installation](/get-started/install-the-cli#alethia-update) for
the behavior of each install channel.

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: alethia open
records.text:
Open the Alethia web console (default) or the docs in your browser. Aliases: `docs`, `dashboard`.

alethia open # opens the active organization's page
alethia open --project boutique # opens that project
alethia open docs # opens the documentation
alethia open console # explicit

 Argument / Flag Default Description 
 ---------- --------- ------------- 
 `[console\ docs]` `console` Which surface to open. Defaults to the console; the `docs` alias defaults to the documentation. 
 `--project` — Open a project's page instead of the organization's, by project name or id. The URL is built from the console's own route tree, so a route rename fails the build rather than the link. 

`alethia docs` (the alias) defaults to the docs target. The argument is optional and has a default,
so `alethia open --no-input` opens the console rather than asking — this is the one shell value a
person supplies, and it is answered rather than prompted for.

The console target opens the **active organization's** page, and `--project` opens a project under
it. Both URLs are built from the route tree the console itself declares
(`packages/core/routing`, generated from `apps/console/app/(private)/**` and checked

records.title: Identity & Global Options
records.heading: alethia completion
records.text:
Generate a shell completion script (standard Cobra completion).

alethia completion bash
alethia completion zsh
alethia completion fish
alethia completion powershell

Follow the script's own header comments to install it for your shell — for example, source it from
your shell profile or drop it into your completions directory.

records.title: Command Reference
records.text: Command Reference. Complete reference for all alethia CLI commands organized by group.

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: Command Reference
records.text:
alethia organizes its commands into groups (`connector`, `project`, `runner`, `jobs`, `cluster`,
`org`, `members`, `teams`, `channels`, `alerts`, `roles`, `grants`, `sso`, `fleet`,
`classification`, `ops`), a set of read-only inspection groups (`repo`, `cloud`, `agent`, `addon`,
`chart`, `iac`, `cost`, `drift`, `staged`, `verify`, `probes`, `protection`, `promotion`), plus top-level
auth (`login`/`logout`/`init`), identity
(`whoami`/`config`/`open`), `billing`, `usage`, `activity`, and utility commands. All commands
communicate with the Alethia [Console](/reference/glossary) API — they never run
[OpenTofu](/reference/glossary) (the `tofu` binary) locally. Provisioning (`tofu plan`/`apply`/
`destroy`) happens on a [Runner](/concepts/runner); the CLI only queues and observes it.

Every command also accepts the [global flags](/reference/cli/identity#output-formats) `-o, --output ` and `--no-input`.

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: Command Tree
records.text:
alethia
├── init [-f alethia.yaml] [--project ] [--region ] [--cloud-account ] [--skip-manifest]
│ # first-run: control-plane URL, login, and an alethia.yaml
├── up [-f alethia.yaml] [--project ] [--region ] [--cloud-account ] [--runner ] [-y/--yes] [--no-wait]
│ # init + apply: from nothing to a running project
├── apply [-f alethia.yaml] [--runner ] [--env …] [-y/--yes] [--no-wait] # the file → a running project
├── plan [-f alethia.yaml] # what apply would create; writes nothing
├── login [-f/--force] [--web-origin ]
├── logout
├── whoami # current user, active org, role, plan, default runner
├── config # show resolved config + file paths + web-origin source
│ ├── set [key] [value] # key: web-origin — asks when omitted
│ ├── get [web-origin active-org]
│ ├── clear-context # clear the active org
│ └── export [project] [--format ] [--out ] # export a project's resolved config
├── version
├── update # update through Homebrew, Scoop, or a verified standalone release
├── open [console docs] # aliases: docs, dashboard
├── completion [bash zsh fish powershell]
├── org # aliases: orgs
│ ├── list
│ ├── switch [org] # id, slug or name — asks when omitted
│ └── settings # the active org's

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: Interactive Selection
records.text:
When `--project-id` (or `--runner-id`) is omitted from `project plan`, `project apply`, or
`project destroy`, alethia launches an interactive TUI selector — provided stdin is a TTY and
`--no-input` is off. See [TUI Components](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs/blob/dev/docs/contributing/cli-tui.md) for how this works.

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: Connect a Cloud Account
records.text: bash

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: Connect a GCP project (runs the installer in your Cloud Shell)
records.text: alethia connector gcp --project my-gcp-project

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: List connected accounts

alethia connector list

See [Connector Commands](/reference/cli/connector) for AWS and Azure flows.

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: Plan-Review-Apply
records.text: bash

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: 1. Plan
records.text: alethia project plan --project boutique

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: 2. Review what it decided — --latest resolves the job you just started
records.text: alethia jobs logs --latest --follow

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: 3. Apply
records.text:
alethia project apply --project boutique

`--project` takes the project's NAME. Omit it on a terminal and you are asked; `--latest` picks
the most recent job, so no id has to travel from one command's output into the next one's
arguments.

To pin the apply to one specific reviewed plan rather than re-planning, name that plan's job id:

alethia project apply --project boutique --plan-job-id 4f3c2b1a-9d6e-4a3b-8c17-5e2f1a9b7c04

records.heading: Scripting with --wait
records.text: bash

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: Block until plan completes, then apply
records.text:
alethia project plan --project boutique --wait
alethia project apply --project boutique --wait
