records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.text: First-Run Setup (init). One command to point the CLI at a control plane, log in, and write the alethia.yaml this directory applies.

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: First-Run Setup
records.text:
`alethia init` is the guided setup: it picks the **control-plane URL**, persists it, runs the browser
[device-code login](/reference/cli/authentication), and writes an `alethia.yaml` for this directory when there
is none.

Every step is skipped when it is already done, so it is safe to re-run. To go all the way to a
running project in one command, use [`alethia up`](/reference/cli/plan-and-apply#alethia-up), which is
this command and `alethia apply` together.

alethia init

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Choose the control-plane URL
records.text:
A form asks for the **control-plane URL**, pre-filled with the current value — the hosted
`alethialabs.io` by default, or your self-hosted / dev origin. The entered value is validated
(must be `http`/`https` with a host) and saved with the trailing slash stripped.

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Log in
records.text:
The device-code flow runs immediately: the CLI opens ` /cli/login?device_code= ` in your
browser and polls ` /api/auth/cli/exchange` until you approve, then writes the tokens. See
[Authentication](/reference/cli/authentication) for the full RFC 8628 flow. A machine that is already signed
in skips this step.

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Write an alethia.yaml
records.text:
When the current directory has no manifest, `init` writes one: the project's name, the cloud
account by its **label**, the region, and the environments with their placements. That file is
what [`alethia apply`](/reference/cli/plan-and-apply) reads.

A directory that already has one is left alone, so re-running `init` is safe. Pass
`--skip-manifest` to do the machine setup by itself.

 

`init` skips whatever is already done — the login included, so adding a manifest to a second
directory does not open a browser. Use [`alethia login --force`](/reference/cli/authentication) to sign in
again deliberately.

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Flags
records.text:
What the manifest declares:

{/* fieldspec: alethia init manifest */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 ------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -------------------- 
 Manifest Where to write the manifest (default: ./alethia.yaml) `--file` 
 Project name Name for the project the manifest declares (asked for on a terminal when omitted) `--project` 
 Region Cloud region to provision into `--region` 
 Cloud account Cloud account to link, by its LABEL or its id `--cloud-account` 
 Stage Stage for the environment it declares `--stage` 
 Machine type Machine type for the cluster nodes, e.g. t3.xlarge (needs a cloud account; not with --node-size) `--instance-type` 
 Node size Node size as vCPUxGiB, e.g. 4x16, mapped to the nearest machine type (not with --instance-type) `--node-size` 
 Machine setup only Set up the CLI without writing a manifest `--skip-manifest` 

`--instance-type` or `--node-size` (one of the two) writes the node shape into the file as a
`cluster` component on each `dedicated` environment. Without either, the file has no `cluster`
component, and the cluster gets the catalog's default mach

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: How the control-plane URL resolves
records.text:
The CLI resolves the origin in this precedence — highest first:

 B[persisted config web-origin]
 B --> C[hosted default alethialabs.io]
`} />

- **`ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN`** — an environment variable, wins for the current shell. Handy for CI or a
 throwaway override without touching the config file.
- **Persisted `web-origin`** — what `alethia init`, `alethia config set web-origin `, and
 `alethia login --web-origin ` write. Stored in the on-disk CLI config.
- **Hosted default** — the built-in `alethialabs.io` origin, used when neither of the above is set.

`alethia config` shows the resolved origin **and its source** (`env` / `config` / `default`), plus
the on-disk config and credentials paths:

alethia config
alethia config get web-origin # just the resolved origin

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Equivalent one-shots
records.text:
`init` is convenience glue. Any of these do the same job piecemeal:

bash

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Set the origin once, then log in
records.text:
alethia config set web-origin https://alethia.internal.example.com
alethia login

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Or set-and-log-in in a single command (persists the origin, then runs the device flow)
records.text: alethia login --web-origin https://alethia.internal.example.com

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Per-shell override without persisting (e.g. dev / CI)
records.text:
alethia login

 
`init`'s **URL prompt** honors `--no-input`: with prompting disabled it takes `--web-origin` if you
passed one, and otherwise keeps the already-resolved origin without asking. The **login** step still
needs a browser to approve the device code — for a fully non-interactive machine, use a
[service-account token](/reference/cli/authentication#running-in-ci) instead of logging in at all. See
[Configuration](/reference/cli/configuration).

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Where things are stored
records.text:
`init` writes to the standard per-user config directory (`os.UserConfigDir()/alethia/`): the
control-plane URL and active-org context to the CLI config file, and the login tokens to a separate
credentials file. `alethia config` prints both exact paths. See
[Configuration](/reference/cli/configuration) for the file formats and
[Authentication](/reference/cli/authentication) for token lifetimes and refresh.

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Authentication](/reference/cli/authentication) — the device-code flow, token refresh, `logout`.
- [Configuration](/reference/cli/configuration) — config keys, env vars, file locations.
- [Command Reference](/reference/cli) — the full command tree.

records.title: Job Commands
records.text: Job Commands. List, stream logs, and cancel infrastructure jobs.

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: Job Commands
records.text:
Monitor and manage provision jobs from the terminal. For how jobs work internally, see [Job queue](/concepts/job-queue).

 
There is no `alethia jobs wait` command. To block until a job finishes, pass `-w/--wait` to the
command that queues it — `project plan apply destroy` and `runner deploy destroy`. See
[Plan & Apply](/reference/cli/plan-and-apply).

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: Choosing the job
records.text:
`jobs get`, `jobs logs` and `jobs cancel` each act on one job. The id is optional, and there are
three ways to say which job you mean:

alethia jobs logs 8f3c2a1e-9d40-4b1e-b0a7-5c2f6e83d411 # an id you already have
alethia jobs logs --latest --follow # the most recent job — no id needed
alethia jobs logs # a picker, on a terminal

`--latest` is the one to use in a script: it needs no terminal, so it works under `--no-input`.
Narrow it until it names one job.

 Flag Description 
 ------ ------------- 
 `--latest` Act on the most recent matching job instead of naming one. Works with `--no-input`. 
 `--type` Narrow to a job type: `PLAN`, `DEPLOY`, `DESTROY`, and the rest of the table below. 
 `--status` Narrow to a status — one of the [STATUS lifecycle](#alethia-jobs-list) values. 
 `--project` Narrow to a project, by name or by an id prefix. 

The search covers the 50 most recent jobs, newest first. A `--type` or `--status` value outside
the enum is refused, and the message lists the values that exist.

Two combinations are refused rather than guessed:

- An id **and** `--latest`. Both name a job, so obeying one would make the other a lie.
- An id **and** a narrowing flag. `jobs log

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: alethia jobs list
records.text:
List jobs for the active organization.

alethia jobs list # every job, newest first
alethia jobs list --status PROCESSING # only what is running now
alethia jobs list --limit 50 -o json # a page a script can read

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--status` No Filter by status — one of the STATUS lifecycle values below. 
 `-n`, `--limit` No Jobs per page (default `20`). 

On a terminal, and only when you did not name a `--status` yourself, the command asks which slice
of the lifecycle you want before it draws the table. **Every status** is the first option, so
pressing Enter gives the unfiltered list. Nothing else is asked: the page size is the one question
the table itself already answers, because it pages.

Anything that is not a person reading a table — `-o json`, a pipe, `--no-input`, a redirected
terminal — is served the flags exactly as given and is never asked. `--status` sets everything the
picker can choose, so no script is worse off for the question it never sees.

Output:

TYPE STATUS PROJECT RUNNER CREATED DURATION
Plan SUCCESS api-backend fleet-hcloud-1 2 min ago 1m 12s
Deploy PROCESSING api-backend fleet-hcloud-1 30 sec ago 28s…
Destroy Q

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: alethia jobs get
records.text:
Get detailed information about one job.

alethia jobs get # a picker, on a terminal
alethia jobs get --latest --type PLAN # the newest plan — works in a script

The job id is an optional positional. See [Choosing the job](#choosing-the-job) for the three ways
to name one.

Shows: type, status, assigned Runner, all timestamps, the Elench `verify_result` summary on
PLAN/DEPLOY jobs, the monthly cost estimate, and the error message (if failed). Add `-o json` for
the full execution metadata (OpenTofu outputs, cost data).

Timestamps are UTC, written the way the console writes them: `9 Mar 2026, 15:04`.

The `Verify` line here is a one-line summary — a verdict and a count. To check the receipt's
signature, see what it is sealed to, or read the per-control report behind that verdict, use
[`alethia verify receipt`](/reference/cli/verify) and `alethia verify show`.

The `Cost estimate` line is the Infracost breakdown the Runner attached to the job, as a monthly
rate: `$124.56/mo (12 priced, 3 free)`. A total under one unit reads `<$1/mo` rather than
rounding to something that looks free.

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: alethia jobs logs
records.text:
Stream job logs to the terminal.

alethia jobs logs --follow # a picker, then stream what it chose
alethia jobs logs --latest --follow # the most recent job — no id needed

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `job_id` No Job ID (positional). Omit it and use `--latest` or the picker. 
 `-f`, `--follow` No Continuously stream new log entries (like `tail -f`) 

Plus the selector flags from [Choosing the job](#choosing-the-job).

Without `--follow`, prints all existing logs and exits. With `--follow`, the command blocks and prints new log lines as the Runner writes them. Logs include `tofu` (OpenTofu) plan/apply output, resource creation progress, and error messages.

When the CLI picked the job for you, it names which one on **stderr** before the output starts, so
`alethia jobs logs --latest grep Error` still gets only the logs.

Press `Ctrl+C` to stop following.

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: alethia jobs cancel
records.text:
Cancel a queued or in-progress job.

alethia jobs cancel # a picker over the cancellable jobs
alethia jobs cancel --latest --type DEPLOY --yes # scripted: skip the confirmation

Cancelling is destructive, so it asks before acting. In a pipeline there is no terminal to ask, so
`--yes` is **required** — without it the command fails rather than cancelling silently.

When `--latest` chose the job, the command names it: in the confirmation on a terminal, and on
stderr before it acts when `--yes` skipped the confirmation. A cancellation you cannot check is
not a confirmation.

Unless you pass `--status` yourself, `--latest` and the picker consider only the jobs that can
still be cancelled — the non-terminal half of the STATUS lifecycle. Without that, a plan that
finished a second ago is "the most recent job", and `--latest --yes` would either fail on the
control plane's refusal or cancel something you did not mean while the deploy kept running.

Sets the job status to CANCELLED. If the job is currently being executed by a Runner, the Runner detects the cancellation on its next status check and terminates the `tofu` process gracefully.

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: Waiting for jobs
records.text:
To block on a job from a script, queue it with `-w/--wait` rather than polling:

bash

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: Plan and block until it finishes, then apply that exact plan and block again
records.text:
alethia project plan --project-id $ID --wait
PLAN_JOB=$(alethia jobs get --latest --type PLAN --project $ID -o json jq -r .id)
alethia project apply --project-id $ID --plan-job-id $PLAN_JOB --wait

On success, `--wait` prints the job's cost estimate through the same renderer `jobs get` uses.

`--plan-job-id` is what makes the second command an *apply of the first one's plan*: the Runner
checks the referenced PLAN job succeeded and downloads its artifact. Drop it and the DEPLOY
re-plans from scratch against whatever the cloud looks like by then, which is the review window
the flag exists to close. The id comes out of `jobs get --latest`, so nothing is copied by hand.

See [Plan & Apply](/reference/cli/plan-and-apply) for the full workflow.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.text: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity). Manage notification channels and alert rules, and read the delivery/activity log, from the alethia CLI.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: Notifications
records.text:
Alethia's notification system has three parts, all manageable from the CLI:

- **Notification channels** are delivery destinations — webhook, email, Slack, PagerDuty, and more —
 that alert rules fan out to.
- **Alert rules** bind product events (event-key patterns) to one or more channels.
- The **activity log** is a durable record of every action, denial, and alert delivery.

All commands operate on the **active organization**, which you change with `alethia org switch`.
Pass `--org ` to scope a single invocation to a different
organization — it is refused with `403` if you are not a member of it. Every command accepts the global
[`-o, --output `](/reference/cli/identity#output-formats) flag.

 
Alerts require a **Pro plan or higher**. Channel secrets (webhook/Slack URLs, PagerDuty routing
keys) are encrypted at rest and never returned by the API — the CLI only shows whether a secret is
configured.
 

 
**Nothing here asks you to copy an id.** `channels verify`, `channels delete` and `alerts delete`
each take the record's **name** as readily as its id, and take nothing at all at a terminal — they
show you what exists and you pick. `alerts create --channel` resolves a channel name

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia channels list
records.text:
Lists the active organization's notification channels. On a TTY this opens the interactive table;
with `--output json csv` (or `--no-input`) it prints a static table.

alethia channels list
alethia channels list -o json

Columns: **Name**, **Type**, **Verified**, **Enabled**, **ID**. The command takes no input of its
own; only the [global flags](/reference/cli) apply.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia channels create
records.text:
Creates a channel. The destination depends on the type; the endpoint is **verified before the
channel is saved** (a channel never exists unverified).

Every value is optional on the command line. At a terminal you are asked for whatever you left
out — and the **type decides which destination question you get**, so a PagerDuty channel is never
asked for a webhook URL. Under `--no-input` the flags are a complete substitute for that form.

 Type Destination it asks for 
 ---- ----------------------- 
 `email` one or more `--recipient ` 
 `pagerduty` `--routing-key ` 
 every other type `--url ` (optionally `--signing-secret`) 

The nine types come from the product's own `alert_channel_type` set: `webhook`, `email`, `slack`,
`rocketchat`, `discord`, `teams`, `mattermost`, `googlechat`, `pagerduty`. `--type --help` prints
that list rather than an abbreviation of it.

bash

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: Answer everything at a terminal
records.text: alethia channels create

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: Slack/webhook
records.text: alethia channels create "Ops Slack" --type slack --url https://hooks.slack.com/services/XXX

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: Email (repeat --recipient for multiple)
records.text: alethia channels create "On-call" --type email --recipient sre@example.com --recipient lead@example.com

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: PagerDuty
records.text:
alethia channels create "PD" --type pagerduty --routing-key R0UT1NGKEY

{/* fieldspec: alethia channels create */}

 Field What it is Set with 
 ------- ------------ ---------- 
 Name What this destination is, so a list of channels is a list of destinations `[name]` 
 Type Which integration delivers it; it decides which destination is asked for next `--type` 
 Recipients Where an email channel delivers; repeat the flag, or separate them with commas `--recipient` 
 Webhook URL Where a webhook or chat channel posts; the endpoint is called before the channel is saved `--url` 
 Signing secret Optional shared secret the receiver checks the delivery signature against `--signing-secret` 
 Routing key The PagerDuty Events API integration key the incident is raised against `--routing-key`

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia channels verify
records.text:
Sends a synthetic test event through the channel and marks it verified.

alethia channels verify
alethia channels verify "Ops Slack"
alethia channels verify 3f1c8a2b

{/* fieldspec: alethia channels verify */}

 Field What it is Set with 
 ------- ------------ ---------- 
 Channel The channel to send a test event through, by name or id; omit it to choose from the list `[channel]`

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia channels delete
records.text:
Deletes a channel (prompts for confirmation, and the prompt **names the channel** rather than
asking about "this channel"). Alert rules bound to it lose this destination; delivery history is
preserved.

alethia channels delete
alethia channels delete "Ops Slack"
alethia channels delete 3f1c8a2b --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia channels delete */}

 Field What it is Set with 
 ------- ------------ ---------- 
 Channel The channel to remove, by name or id; omit it to choose from the list `[channel]` 

 
Deleting is destructive, so with `--no-input` (or a non-terminal stdin) it **fails** rather than
prompting. Pass `--yes` in a script.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia alerts list
records.text:
Lists the active organization's alert rules with their bound channel count.

alethia alerts list
alethia alerts list -o json

Columns: **Name**, **Severity**, **Events**, **Channels**, **Enabled**, **ID**. The command takes
no input of its own.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia alerts create
records.text:
Creates a rule binding one or more **event-key patterns** (e.g. `system.job.failed`,
`authz.*.denied`) to notification channels. Repeat `--event` and `--channel` for multiple values.

`--channel` takes a channel's **name** as readily as its id, so a rule can be created without first
copying an id out of `channels list`. Omit the channels entirely at a terminal and you get a
multi-select over the org's channels.

bash

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: Answer everything at a terminal
records.text:
alethia alerts create

alethia alerts create "Job failures" --event system.job.failed --channel "Ops Slack" --severity critical

{/* fieldspec: alethia alerts create */}

 Field What it is Set with 
 ------- ------------ ---------- 
 Name What this rule is for, so a list of rules is a list of intentions `[name]` 
 Event patterns Which event keys fire it, e.g. system.job.failed or authz.*.denied `--event` 
 Channels Where it delivers, by channel name or id; omit them to choose from the list `--channel` 
 Severity How loud the delivery is; one of the alert_severity values `--severity` 

The severities are the product's own `alert_severity` set: `info`, `warning` (the default), and
`critical`. A value outside it is refused with the three named, rather than passed to the server.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia alerts delete
records.text:
Deletes an alert rule (prompts for confirmation, naming the rule). Matching events will no longer
be routed.

alethia alerts delete
alethia alerts delete "Job failures"
alethia alerts delete a1b2c3d4 --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia alerts delete */}

 Field What it is Set with 
 ------- ------------ ---------- 
 Alert rule The rule to remove, by name or id; omit it to choose from the list `[rule]` 

 
As with `channels delete`, this is destructive: with `--no-input` it fails unless `--yes` is passed.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia activity
records.text:
Reads the active organization's delivery/activity log — every recorded action and denial, newest
first, including alert deliveries.

alethia activity
alethia activity -n 200
alethia activity -o json

Omit `-n` on a terminal and you are asked how many rows, from a short ladder with the cursor already
on the default — so Enter reads the same 50 entries it read before. The value has a default, so
nothing is ever refused for omitting it: `activity --no-input`, and anything running where a prompt
cannot be shown, reads 50 without a question, and `-n` answers it outright either way.

{/* fieldspec: alethia activity */}

 Field What it is Set with 
 ------- ------------ ---------- 
 Rows How many entries to read back, newest first `--limit` 

Columns: **Time**, **Actor**, **Action**, **Resource**, **Decision** (`allow` / `deny`), and
**Reason** — which is the point of a deny row, so it is always shown, and renders as `—` when the
entry carries none. **Time** reads as an age (`3 minutes ago`) inside a week and as a date beyond
it, and **Resource** pairs the kind with a shortened id: `project 4f3c1a92…`.

Those are renderings for a person, and `-o csv` gives a script the values instead: **T

records.title: Ops Commands
records.text: Ops Commands. Break-glass incident-recovery verbs — audited, reason-gated, cross-tenant actions for on-call operators.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: Ops Commands
records.text:
The `ops` group is the terminal-first **break-glass** surface: privileged incident-recovery
actions for on-call operators. Every verb hits the same audited `/api/breakglass/*` endpoints as
the operator UI, with the same bearer [CLI token](/reference/cli/authentication) and the same append-only
audit trail.

 
The entire surface is gated behind the `ALETHIA_BREAKGLASS_ENABLED` flag **and** the
`BREAKGLASS_OPERATORS` server-side allowlist. A non-operator — or a deployment that has not enabled
break-glass — is refused with a 403/404. Membership in an organization is **not** the wall: these
endpoints are cross-tenant and bypass row-level security, so the operator allowlist is the only gate.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: The break-glass model
records.text:
Four rules hold for every action.

- **Audited.** An append-only audit record is written *before* the act. Every verb requires a
 `--reason` of at least eight characters, and it is what the next person reading the audit has to
 go on.
- **Typed-confirm.** A mutating action echoes the exact resource id back to the server; a mismatch
 is refused. The CLI sends this confirmation for you.
- **Confirmed at the terminal.** Every action that changes something names the resource and the
 consequence and waits for you. `--yes` opts in ahead of time, which is what a runbook or a
 pipeline passes. With prompts unavailable and no `--yes`, the command exits non-zero having
 changed nothing — it never exits `0` having done nothing.
- **Two-person approval for high-blast actions.** `force-release-lock`, `state-surgery`, and
 `orphan-clean` require an `--approval` token minted by a **different** operator through
 [`alethia ops approve`](#alethia-ops-approve). The server enforces that the approver and the actor
 are different people.

Each action opens a fresh time-boxed break-glass session before it runs, records the reason, then
executes against the single audited execute endpoint. The session op

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: Nothing is copied between commands
records.text:
Every id in this group is an optional positional or an optional flag. Give one and it is passed
through exactly as typed, with no listing request made for it. Give none on a terminal and the
command asks:

- `inspect-job`, `retry-job` and `cancel-job` offer your organization's recent jobs, rendered by
 the [`jobs`](/reference/cli/jobs) group's own line renderer so a job reads the same in both.
- `drain-runner` and `restart-runner` offer every runner, including the offline ones — a drain is
 aimed at the runner that is wrong.
- `unstick-env` offers a project, then its environments, and starts the compare-and-swap
 precondition at the status the environment is actually in.
- `orphan-detect` and `orphan-clean` offer your projects.
- `approve` offers the actions that take an approval, read from the same catalog the server
 enforces.

The one value you still type from elsewhere is `--approval`, and that is the point of it: a
two-person token is minted by another operator on another terminal and handed to you. A token this
CLI could fetch for you would not be two-person.

A state key and a Stripe event id have no listing anywhere, so those two are asked as questions
rather than offered a

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: Blast radius
records.text:
Each verb is labelled with its blast radius in its help text. The labels come from the server's
break-glass catalog, so they are the same ones the dispatcher enforces.

 Blast Verbs Confirms 
 ------- ------- ---------- 
 none (read-only) `inspect-job`, `orphan-detect` no — nothing changes 
 low `retry-job`, `cancel-job`, `drain-runner`, `replay-webhook` yes 
 medium `unstick-env`, `restart-runner` yes 
 HIGH (two-person) `force-release-lock`, `state-surgery`, `orphan-clean` yes, plus `--approval`

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops
records.text:
The group itself is runnable and prints the verb list with each one's blast radius, which is the
fastest way to see what break-glass can do without reading this page.

alethia ops

It takes no flags and performs no action — listing the surface is not itself a privileged act, so
it needs neither a `--reason` nor an audit record.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops session
records.text:
Open a standalone time-boxed break-glass session. The action verbs open their own session; this is
for inspecting or warming a session, or for scripts that reuse one.

alethia ops session --reason incident-1234-triage

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops session */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason` 

Prints the session id, the resolved operator, and the session's expiry.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops approve
records.text:
Mint a single-use, TTL'd, two-person approval bound to a high-blast action and resource. Run this as
the **second** operator; the acting operator then passes the printed id as `--approval`.

alethia ops approve --reason incident-1234-signoff
alethia ops approve state_surgery projects/acme/prod.tfstate --reason incident-1234-signoff

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops approve */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Action Which high-blast action this approval lets the other operator perform `[action]` 
 Resource The exact resource the approval is bound to; a different one is refused `[resource-id]` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason` 

The action must be one that takes an approval: `force_release_state_lock`, `state_surgery`, or
`orphan_clean`. The server answers `400` for any other one, so the CLI refuses it first and names
the three.

Prints the approval id, the action and resource it is bound to, the approver, and its expiry.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops inspect-job
records.text:
Read a job's full row cross-tenant. Read-only (blast: none), so it asks for no confirmation and
carries no `--yes`.

alethia ops inspect-job --reason incident-1234-deploy-hung
alethia ops inspect-job 8f3c2a1b-77de-4c05-9a41-2b8e6a1d40f7 --reason incident-1234-deploy-hung

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops inspect-job */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Job The job to read; pick one, or pass an id an alert gave you `[job-id]` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason` 

The picker lists your own organization's recent jobs. Break-glass reaches jobs that listing does
not, which is why an id given on the command line skips it entirely.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops retry-job
records.text:
Re-enqueue a fresh job from a stuck or failed one (blast: low). The poison counter resets and the
work runs again.

alethia ops retry-job --reason incident-1234-runner-crash
alethia ops retry-job 8f3c2a1b-77de-4c05-9a41-2b8e6a1d40f7 --reason incident-1234-runner-crash --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops retry-job */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Job The job to re-enqueue; a fresh job is created and the poison counter resets `[job-id]` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason`

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops cancel-job
records.text:
Cancel a job and signal its Runner to stop mid-flight (blast: low). Work already applied is not
rolled back.

alethia ops cancel-job --reason incident-1234-wrong-project
alethia ops cancel-job 8f3c2a1b-77de-4c05-9a41-2b8e6a1d40f7 --reason incident-1234-wrong-project --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops cancel-job */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Job The job to cancel; its runner is signalled to stop mid-flight `[job-id]` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason`

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops unstick-env
records.text:
Move a stuck environment to a target status through the `set_env_status` compare-and-swap primitive —
never a raw `UPDATE` (blast: medium). A compare-and-swap miss is refused, which is what makes this
safe to run against an environment that is moving under you.

alethia ops unstick-env --reason incident-1234-stuck-after-crash
alethia ops unstick-env 5c1f0a92-3d77-4a10-b8e2-7f9d4c6b1a03 --from PROVISIONING,QUEUED --to FAILED --reason incident-1234-stuck-after-crash --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops unstick-env */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Environment The environment to move; pick one, or pass its id `[environment-id]` 
 Expected from The statuses the move is allowed to start from; a compare-and-swap miss is refused `--from` 
 Move to The status to move the environment to `--to` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason` 

Both sides are project statuses: `DRAFT`, `QUEUED`, `PROVISIONING`, `ACTIVE`, `FAILED`,
`DESTROYING`, `DESTROYED`. Anything else is refused before the request is made, because the server
refuses it too.

Picked from the list, `--from` starts at the status the environment is in.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops drain-runner
records.text:
Mark an online Runner `DRAINING` so it stops claiming jobs (blast: low). It finishes the jobs it
already holds.

alethia ops drain-runner --reason incident-1234-node-degraded
alethia ops drain-runner e77b1c40-9a2f-4d61-8c33-5b0e2a7f9d41 --reason incident-1234-node-degraded --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops drain-runner */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Runner The runner to drain; it finishes what it holds and claims nothing new `[runner-id]` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason`

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops restart-runner
records.text:
Drain a Runner and wake the scaler to roll a replacement (blast: medium). This runner does not come
back.

alethia ops restart-runner --reason incident-1234-wedged-runner
alethia ops restart-runner e77b1c40-9a2f-4d61-8c33-5b0e2a7f9d41 --reason incident-1234-wedged-runner --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops restart-runner */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Runner The runner to roll; it is drained and the scaler wakes to replace it `[runner-id]` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason`

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops force-release-lock
records.text:
Force-release a stranded [OpenTofu](/reference/glossary) state lock (blast: HIGH, two-person). It
rotates the fencing token and bumps the generation — never a naive delete — so a writer still
holding the lock is fenced out mid-apply.

alethia ops force-release-lock projects/acme/prod.tfstate --approval 6b21d8f4-0c5e-4a93-9f27-3d81b6e5c704 --reason incident-1234-runner-died-holding-lock --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops force-release-lock */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 State key The locked state object; the fencing token rotates so a zombie writer is fenced out `[state-key]` 
 Approval The approval id a second operator read out to you from their own ops approve run `--approval` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason`

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops state-surgery
records.text:
Queue a privileged `STATE_SURGERY` job through the normal Runner/state pipeline, with fencing intact
(blast: HIGH, two-person).

alethia ops state-surgery projects/acme/prod.tfstate --approval 6b21d8f4-0c5e-4a93-9f27-3d81b6e5c704 --note import-orphaned-rds --reason incident-1234-failed-apply --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops state-surgery */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 State key The state object the surgery job will operate on `[state-key]` 
 Approval The approval id a second operator read out to you from their own ops approve run `--approval` 
 Repair note What the repair is meant to do; recorded in the audit and read by whoever reviews it `--note` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason` 

The note is the only optional field in the group. It is still asked for on a terminal, because the
person who reads the audit is not the person running this, and "state surgery, no note" is the row
that gets escalated.

 
The runner-side executor ships **inert** (fail-closed): the queued job fails cleanly without
mutating state. See the `STATE_SURGERY` job type in [Job Commands](/reference/cli/jobs).

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops orphan-detect
records.text:
List orphan candidates for a single project. Read-only and run-scoped — never account-wide
(blast: none), so it asks for no confirmation and carries no `--yes`.

alethia ops orphan-detect --reason incident-1234-post-incident-sweep
alethia ops orphan-detect --project 1d4e7c30-8b62-4f95-a70d-9c2e5b1a3f88 --reason incident-1234-post-incident-sweep

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops orphan-detect */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Project The project to scan; detection is run-scoped and never account-wide `--project` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason`

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops orphan-clean
records.text:
Force-destroy detected orphans across clouds (blast: HIGH, two-person) — the most dangerous action.
The resources do not come back.

alethia ops orphan-clean --project 1d4e7c30-8b62-4f95-a70d-9c2e5b1a3f88 --approval 6b21d8f4-0c5e-4a93-9f27-3d81b6e5c704 --reason incident-1234-cleanup-approved --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops orphan-clean */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Project The project whose detected orphans are force-destroyed `--project` 
 Approval The approval id a second operator read out to you from their own ops approve run `--approval` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason` 

 
`orphan-clean` ships **inert**. It refuses unless the deployment is separately armed with
`ALETHIA_BREAKGLASS_ORPHAN_CLEAN_ENABLED`, and even when armed it is unimplemented rather than
performing an unscoped delete.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops replay-webhook
records.text:
Re-dispatch a stored Stripe webhook event through the same idempotent handler the live webhook uses
(blast: low).

alethia ops replay-webhook --reason incident-1234-missed-invoice
alethia ops replay-webhook evt_1P9xKjLkdIwHu7ix --reason incident-1234-missed-invoice --yes
alethia ops replay-webhook evt_1P9xKjLkdIwHu7ix --send-emails --reason incident-1234-missed-invoice --yes

{/* fieldspec: alethia ops replay-webhook */}

 Field What it is Set without the form 
 --- --- --- 
 Stripe event The stored event to re-dispatch through the live idempotent handler `[stripe-event-id]` 
 Re-send emails Branded emails are the one non-idempotent side effect, so they are suppressed unless you ask `--send-emails` 
 Reason Why you are breaking glass; it is written to the immutable audit before the act `--reason` 

The confirmation says which of the two it is about to do. The handler is idempotent; the emails are
not, so the run that re-sends them is named as such.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: Scripting the group
records.text:
Every field above is settable from the command line, so the whole group works with `--no-input`.
The rule is one line: **a value you did not supply is asked for, and if it cannot be asked for the
command tells you which flag or positional would have answered it, and exits non-zero.** The one
exception is `state-surgery`'s `--note`, which is optional: an unattended run gets no note rather
than a refusal.

Two things a script needs to know:

- `--yes` is required on every mutating verb when prompts are unavailable. Without it the command
 exits non-zero and changes nothing, which is the safe answer for a pipeline that reached a
 destructive verb it did not mean to.
- `-o json` prints the payload alone. The styled success line is only rendered for the table
 format, so a break-glass result pipes into `jq` without a sentence in front of it.

 
 One thing still writes to `stdout` ahead of the payload: the loading spinner, which draws its
 frames there rather than on `stderr`. A redirected or piped `-o json` result can therefore begin
 with terminal escape sequences, and `jq` reports `Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 2`.
 Until [#3838](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethiala

records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Job Commands](/reference/cli/jobs) — the `STATE_SURGERY` job type and the job lifecycle.
- [Command Reference](/reference/cli) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.text: Organizations, Members & Teams. Switch the active organization and manage its members and teams from the CLI.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.text:
alethia scopes everything you do — projects, runners, jobs, connectors — to an **active
organization**. The active org is persisted locally (in `~/.config/alethia/config.json`) and sent as
the `X-Alethia-Org` header on every request.

`--org ` targets a different organization for a single invocation, on every command in the CLI
and not only the ones on this page. It sets the `X-Alethia-Org` header, and for `members` and
`teams` — the two commands that address the org in their request path — it sets the org in the path
as well, from the same value. Naming an organization you are not a member of is refused with `403`.
Under a service token the flag must name the token's own organization: a different one is refused
with `403` rather than quietly ignored, so a pipeline cannot believe it is acting on one org while
every write lands in another.

Every command here also accepts the global `--org `,
[`-o, --output `](/reference/cli/identity#output-formats) and `--no-input` flags.

 
Nothing on this page asks you to copy an id out of a previous command. `members remove` takes
`--email`, `teams delete` takes `--name`, and both offer a picker when you name nothing — so
`--no-input` always has

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia org list
records.text:
List the organizations you belong to. The active org is marked in the `Active` column.

alethia org list

Output:

NAME SLUG ROLE PLAN ACTIVE
Acme acme owner pro ◆
Personal you owner free

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia org switch
records.text:
Set the active organization. Pass an org **id, slug, or name**; with no argument, pick one
interactively.

alethia org switch acme
alethia org switch

{/* fieldspec: alethia org switch */}

 Field What it is Flag or argument Name it by 
 ----- ---------- ---------------- ---------- 
 Organization The organization to make active; its id, slug, or name `[org]` — 

The selection is persisted locally and sent as `X-Alethia-Org` on subsequent commands. Clear it with
[`alethia config clear-context`](/reference/cli/configuration#alethia-config).

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia org settings
records.text:
Show the active organization's general settings.

alethia org settings
alethia org settings -o json

Renders a field/value card: **name**, **slug**, **description**, **region** (the org's default
provisioning region), **default env**, and **`terraform`** (the default OpenTofu version). Prints
`Not in an organization (community mode).` when the caller has no real org (personal scope). Backing
call: `GET /cli/org-settings`.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia members list
records.text:
List the members of the active organization: id, email, name, role, and invitation status. The `ID`
column is there for `-o json` and `-o csv` consumers — you never need to copy it by hand.

alethia members list
alethia members list -o json
alethia members list --org org_456

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia members add
records.text:
Invite someone to the active organization. Pass their email and `--role` to run without a terminal;
with neither, the form asks for both and offers the org's own roles — including any custom role.

alethia members add teammate@example.com --role operator
alethia members add

{/* fieldspec: alethia members add */}

 Field What it is Flag or argument Name it by 
 ----- ---------- ---------------- ---------- 
 Email Who to invite; they get an invitation at this address `[email]` — 
 Role What the invited member may do, from the org's roles `--role` — 

`--role` defaults to `member`. A scripted `alethia members add ada@example.com --no-input` keeps
that default; on a terminal the form asks, because the default is rarely what the inviter meant.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia members remove
records.text:
Remove a member. Name them by email, or pick from the org's members; the member id still works if
you have one.

alethia members remove --email teammate@example.com --yes
alethia members remove

{/* fieldspec: alethia members remove */}

 Field What it is Flag or argument Name it by 
 ----- ---------- ---------------- ---------- 
 Member Who to remove; name them by email rather than copying a member id `[member_id]` `--email` 

This is destructive, so it confirms first. `--yes` (or `-y`) skips the prompt and is **required**
with `--no-input` — a scripted removal without it exits non-zero rather than silently doing nothing.
When the CLI picks the member for you, it prints which one on stderr before it asks.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia teams list
records.text:
List the teams in the active organization, with a member count.

alethia teams list
alethia teams list --org org_456

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia teams create
records.text:
Create a team. Pass the name to run without a terminal; with no name, the form asks for one.

alethia teams create platform
alethia teams create

{/* fieldspec: alethia teams create */}

 Field What it is Flag or argument Name it by 
 ----- ---------- ---------------- ---------- 
 Name What the team is called, so a list of teams is a list of purposes `[name]` —

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia teams delete
records.text:
Delete a team. Name it with `--name`, or pick from the org's teams.

alethia teams delete --name platform --yes
alethia teams delete

{/* fieldspec: alethia teams delete */}

 Field What it is Flag or argument Name it by 
 ----- ---------- ---------------- ---------- 
 Team Which team to delete; name it rather than copying a team id `[team_id]` `--name` 

Members keep their org membership but lose the grants the team carried. Destructive, so it confirms;
`--yes` skips the prompt and is required with `--no-input`.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: Flags
records.text:
Flag Where Description 
 ------ ------- ------------- 
 `--org ` every command (global) Operate on this org instead of the active one, for one invocation. 
 `--role ` `members add` Role for the invited member. Default `member`. 
 `--email ` `members remove` Name the member by address instead of a member id. 
 `--name ` `teams delete` Name the team instead of a team id. 
 `-y, --yes` `members remove`, `teams delete` Skip the confirmation prompt. Required with `--no-input`.

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.text: Plan & Apply. Queue plan, deploy, and destroy jobs from the CLI.

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: Plan & Apply
records.text:
One file describes a project; two commands take it from a file to a running cluster. Nothing has
to be copied out of another command's output: the cloud account is named by its **label**, the
runner by its **name**, and every environment by the name the file gives it.

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: alethia.yaml
records.text:
The manifest is the whole shape of a project — where it provisions, every environment with its
placement, and the components each environment carries:

project: boutique
cloud:
 account: prod-account # the connector's label, as `alethia connector list` shows it
 region: nbg1
environments:
 - name: prod
 stage: production
 placement: dedicated # owns the Fabric: this is the environment with a cluster
 components:
 cluster:
 node_min_size: 2
 node_max_size: 3
 - name: dev-1
 stage: development
 placement: namespace # placed onto prod's Fabric, no new cluster
 namespace: boutique-dev-1
 components:
 repositories:
 apps_destination_repo: https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-examples
 apps_path: examples/online-boutique/overlays/dev-1
 databases:
 - name: orders
 engine: postgres

 Key What it is 
 --- --- 
 `project` The project's name. Unique in the organization, so `apply` finds an existing project by it. 
 `cloud.account` The cloud account's label (or its id). Omit it to create an unlinked project. 
 `cloud.region` The region to provision into. 
 `iac.version` OpenTofu version to pin. Optional; the server defaults it. 
 `environments[].name` The environment's name. 
 `environme

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: alethia apply
records.text:
Create whatever the file declares that does not exist yet, show the plan, and deploy every
environment.

alethia apply # ./alethia.yaml, asks before applying
alethia apply --yes --no-input # in a pipeline
alethia apply --runner my-box # deploy with a named runner
alethia apply --env dev-1 # create everything, deploy only dev-1

▸ Reading alethia.yaml · boutique · hetzner/nbg1
 + project boutique
 prod dedicated + environment + cluster
 dev-1 namespace + environment + repositories + databases/orders
 1 project to create · 2 environments · 3 components
Apply these changes? Yes
 ✓ created project boutique
 ✓ added cluster in prod
 ✓ added repositories in dev-1
 ✓ added databases/orders in dev-1
▸ Deploying prod (job 4f3c2b1a-…)
 ✓ Job completed successfully
▸ Deploying dev-1 (job 8a1d0e77-…)
 ✓ Job completed successfully

✓ boutique is up.

`apply` is idempotent. Re-run it on a project that already matches the file and it creates
nothing, marks each environment `=`, and deploys again. It **never deletes**: an environment on the
server that the file does not mention is listed as left alone, not torn down. What it cannot
reconcile — an existing environment whose stage or placement diffe

records.heading: alethia up
records.text:
The whole first run in one command: sign in, attach nothing (see below), write the manifest, apply
it. Every step is skipped when it is already done, so it resumes wherever the last run stopped.

alethia up # asks for what it needs
alethia up --project boutique --region nbg1 --cloud-account prod-account --yes --no-input

 a cloud account one is connected — **otherwise `up` stops**, see below

 the apply never; that is the point 

With the manifest already present and an account connected, `alethia up` **is** `alethia apply`.

 
 `up` cannot attach a cloud account for you. Each cloud has its own keyless flow with its own
 arguments — `alethia connector aws gcp azure alibaba hetzner` — so `up` stops and names them
 rather than growing a sixth version that would drift from the five.

records.text:
The same comparison, with the writes left out: what `apply` would create, what already matches,
and anything it would refuse. Nothing is written and no job is queued.

alethia plan
alethia plan --file staging.yaml --output json

{/* fieldspec: alethia plan */}

 Manifest The alethia.yaml to plan (default: ./alethia.yaml) `--file` 

The per-environment OpenTofu plan runs inside every deploy. To queue one on its own — for a
pipeline that gates on it — use `alethia project plan` below.

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: The project job commands
records.text:
These `project` subcommands queue infrastructure operations that [Runners](/concepts/runner) execute. They
implement the Plan-Review-Apply workflow from the terminal, one environment at a time. The same
workflow in the console is [Plan and apply in the console](/guides/jobs/plan-and-apply).

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: alethia project plan
records.text:
Queue an [OpenTofu](/reference/glossary) plan job — the Runner runs `tofu plan`.

alethia project plan # asks which project, then which runner
alethia project plan --project boutique --env prod --runner eu-box --wait # scripted: names all three, blocks on the job

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project` No Project to plan, by **name** or id. Omitted on a terminal, a picker asks. 
 `--project-id` No Project id. Prefer `--project`, which also takes the id. Passing both is refused. 
 `--env` No Environment name to plan. Omitted, the project's default environment. 
 `--runner` No Runner to execute the job, by **name** or id. Omitted, a picker asks on a terminal; under `--no-input` the server places the job. 
 `--runner-id` No Runner id. Prefer `--runner`, which also takes the name. Passing both is refused. 
 `-w`, `--wait` No Block until the job completes 

On success, prints the job ID. Stream the plan output with
`alethia jobs logs --latest --project boutique --follow` — nothing has to be copied between the two
commands. Narrow it to the project you just planned: an unnarrowed `alethia jobs logs --latest`
takes the most recent job **the organization

records.text:
Queue a deployment (apply) job.

alethia project apply # asks which project, then which runner
alethia project apply --project boutique --env prod --latest-plan --wait # scripted: applies the plan just reviewed

 Flag Required Description

 `--project` No Project to deploy, by **name** or id. Omitted on a terminal, a picker asks. 
 `--project-id` No Project id. Prefer `--project`, which also takes the id. Passing both is refused. 
 `--env` No Environment name to deploy. Omitted, the project's default environment.

 `--latest-plan` No Apply the project's most recent `PLAN` job. Prefer this to `--plan-job-id`. 
 `--plan-job-id` No Bind the apply to the plan a prior PLAN job produced, by that job's id. 
 `-w`, `--wait` No Block until the job completes 

Either flag makes the apply use the exact plan you reviewed. If the project's configuration
changed since that plan was generated, the job fails with a
[confi

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: Destroying an environment that other environments run on
records.text:
A `dedicated` environment owns its cluster. `namespace` and `vcluster` environments placed on that
cluster run inside it, and their own teardown needs the cluster to still exist. So while any of them
is live, destroying the `dedicated` environment is **refused**, and the error names each one:

Environment "prod" owns the cluster that 2 other environments are still placed on:
dev-1 (namespace, ACTIVE), staging (vcluster, FAILED). ...
Re-run with --cascade to see every environment it would destroy and confirm

An environment that was never applied (`DRAFT`) or is already `DESTROYED` does not count. Destroying
a `namespace` or `vcluster` environment is never refused for this reason.

Either destroy the listed environments first, or pass `--cascade`. It prints what it will destroy,
then asks:

Will destroy, in order: dev-1 (namespace), staging (vcluster, failed), prod (dedicated, owns the cluster)

The order is enforced by the Console, not by timing: the DESTROY of `prod` stays `QUEUED`, and no
Runner can start it, until no live environment is left on its cluster. If the destroy of `dev-1` or
`staging` fails, `prod` keeps waiting. `--wait` stops at the failed job and names the two ways

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: Interactive Selection
records.text:
`plan`, `apply` and `destroy` each ask for what you did not name, so none of the three needs an id
typed at it:

1. With neither `--project` nor `--project-id`, a picker lists the projects and you choose one.
2. With the runner unnamed, a second picker lists your runners, marking each one online, draining or
 offline. **Any available** is its first option, so pressing Enter leaves the job for the server
 to place.

Neither picker is shown under `--no-input` or when stdin is not a terminal. There, name the project
with `--project` and the runner with `--runner` — both take the name, so a script never has to hold
an id — or leave the runner unset for the server to place. A name no runner has is refused locally,
listing the names that do exist; a name two runners share is refused naming both ids, rather than
picking one for you.

See [TUI Components](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs/blob/dev/docs/contributing/cli-tui.md) for details on the interactive selectors.
